2a494ad604ec9734: In what sounds like an avian riff on The Wire, scientists equipped seabirds with audio recorders in order to listen in on their interactions with fishing vessels across the world’s oceans, according to a study published on Wednesday in Science Advances.

The approach exposed a large number of so-called “unseen” vessels that did not have their location trackers switched on. Many vessels are required to continuously signal their location using the Automatic Identification System (AIS), which openly broadcasts a ship’s location, similar to flight tracking. But AIS can be disabled for legitimate reasons—such as evading pirates—or with more nefarious motivations, such as concealment of illegal fishing activities.

The new study was not designed to interrogate why any particular vessel switched off its AIS tracker. However, the discovery that seabirds are regularly interacting with unseen ships can shed light on broader efforts to monitor commercial fisheries, while also revealing new insights about seabird behavior, especially their risk of becoming “bycatch” when they are fatally trapped in fishing gear.

Unseen vessel activity “is concerning, or at least important, regardless of whether it's legal or illegal,” said Jonathan Rutter, a postdoctoral research fellow at the University of Oxford who led the study, in a call with 404 Media. He added that the recordings were not intended to be used for law-enforcement or surveillance, but that this line of research could become a “powerful tool for improving risk assessment” by recording seabird-vessel interactions that would otherwise be off the map.

Scientists have previously attached audio recorders to birds, such as penguins, to better understand their vocalizations and behavior, and teams have also probed seabird-vessel interactions with bird-borne radar.

<!--kg-card-begin: html--> <!--kg-card-end: html--> Rutter and his colleagues were inspired to combine these approaches by attaching audio recorders to three seabird species—the northern gannet, Balearic shearwater, and Westland petrel—which all frequently interact with fishing vessels. The team tracked the movements of the birds with GPS, and then analyzed whether the audio overlapped with AIS data at the same time and location during recorded interactions.

The recordings showed that about 32 percent of the audio captured by seven gannets in the North Atlantic were from ships with their trackers off, while 12 percent of the audio captured by four shearwaters in the Mediterranean Sea were from unseen vessels. The one petrel in the study interacted with vessels in the South Pacific, but its geolocation device was damaged, so it was not possible to calculate how many ships it encountered had their trackers off.

Rutter noted that the shearwaters were likely often interacting with smaller Mediterranean fishing boats that are not legally required to keep trackers on. However, the gannets encountered larger commercial vessels that are obligated to keep trackers active. While the researchers made a very conservative estimate that these birds visited unseen vessels for about one-third of the total duration of their daily encounters (or, about 22 minutes out of 68 minutes), it may well exceed half of that time.

“The fact that we found at least one third, and probably more than one half, of the audio detections being unseen was pretty surprising,” Rutter said. “This is not the same thing as saying that half of vessels are unseen; it's half of the time that gannets go to vessels, those vessels are unseen.”

“There are multiple reasons this could be,” he continued. “It could be illegal disabling, but at the same time, it could be poor satellite reception. There are lots of reasons that AIS can be off, and we want to emphasize that illegal fishing is a possibility, but that is not actually what we're showing. It's showing that there's a lot we're not seeing.”

Seabirds are attracted to fishing vessels to feed on discarded catch, but many perish during these encounters after becoming tangled in lines or caught on baited hooks. Rutter and his colleagues hope that their study could help to prevent these deadly incidents, while also providing a new tool for monitoring unseen vessel activity.

While this approach could enable real-time vessel detection, the team urged “caution in the use of animals as a fisheries surveillance tool, lest fishers come to mistrust scientists and/or marine animals themselves,” according to the study.

Though environmental and commercial interests are often at odds, there is plenty of collaboration between fisheries and conservation scientists with the goal of sustainable and healthy long-term fish stock. Fisheries that adhere to regulations also have an interest in working with researchers to combat illegal activity by competitors.

In addition, these audio recordings offer a new way to eavesdrop on wild seabird behavior. For example, the petrel’s recordings captured distinct landing and takeoff sequences previously observed in albatrosses, opening a new avenue of research into the flight patterns of this species. The recordings also highlight how human activity has upended food webs, as seabirds have become dependent on fishing vessel waste as a major source of food.

“One of the advantages of this is that we can understand in a more unbiased way how much [seabirds] actually interact with vessels—every day, multiple times a day for all the species we looked at actually, which is crazy if you think about it,” Rutter said.
“They're going out every day and just visiting boats all the time, and that shows the impact that we have on them as humans is really changing their feeding ecology,” he concluded.

b946c695c0817290: Chinese telecom and IT giant Huawei boasted about its advancements in domestic electronic design automation (EDA) software this week, which it needs to accelerate the adoption of homegrown chip manufacturing.
EDA is an umbrella term for software, hardware, and services essential to the planning, design, and production of modern chips.
Today, Cadence Design Systems, Synopsys, and Siemens dominate the industry, but US export controls have restricted Huawei and other blacklisted Chinese businesses' access to their tools.
The US blacklisted Huawei back in 2019 over concerns the telecommunications equipment giant could be forced to inject backdoors into its gear.
Unable to access top EDA tools, Huawei’s chip division, HiSilicon, was forced to develop its own with the help of Phlexing Technology.
This week, Phlexing chairman Qing He detailed the company’s efforts to bring new EDA tools to support Huawei’s so-called Tau Scaling Law design philosophy.
“Tau EDA is the domestic EDA tool chain for Tau chips. It comes from a long, close partnership with Huawei,” he said.
We discussed the tech earlier this year, but in a nutshell, it involves using advanced packaging, specifically 3D hybrid bonding, to achieve higher transistor density for a given area.

The TSMC of China, Semiconductor Manufacturing International Corporation (SMIC), is still years behind Taiwan, South Korea, and the US on process technology. It currently has the ability to mass-produce chips on the equivalent of a 7 nm process.
For comparison, TSMC began producing 5 nm-class products in 2020 and commenced mass production of 2 nm-class chips in late 2025.

So, Huawei aims to use 3D packaging to close the gap, but for this to happen, it first needs tools capable of designing such chips, and that’s just what Phlexing claims to have done with its GloryBolt and GloryEX platforms.

“Traditional EDA has long handled only single processes. Tau EDA needs to integrate and decompose multiple processes,” He said. “Coupling multi-scale, multi-structure, and multi-physics issues called for new analysis tools.”
This, He says, culminated in the co-development of a process design kit (PDK) with Huawei beginning in 2024. These technologies have now gone live.
The development comes as Huawei looks to bring larger, more capable processors to market.

We previously discussed the company’s latest developments around AI accelerators, near packaged optics, networking, and rack systems. Many of these advancements will depend on multi-die chip packages, enabled by EDA tools, like those built by Phlexing. ®

d0d15a6780baf7c7: After four years of work to build a browser engine from scratch, the Ladybird project released its first downloadable alpha on November 23, offering prebuilt versions for macOS and Linux. Previously, curious users had to compile the browser themselves from its source. Now it's an installable package with automatic updating.

Ladybird is most notable for what it isn't: another browser fork. Where Chrome, Edge, Brave, and Opera all run on Google's Blink engine, and Firefox depends on Gecko, Ladybird's rendering engine and its LibJS JavaScript engine were written from scratch. "The engine is our own, built from the ground up, and not a fork," project lead Andreas Kling wrote in Monday's announcement. "The browser around it is modest, but functional."

Nearly the entire modern web currently runs on three browser engines. There's WebKit (Safari), Gecko (Firefox), and the biggest of them all, Blink (Chromium). Those limited options mean that web developers often end up optimizing sites for Chromium specifically, since that's where the majority of traffic is, and as a result, the whole web platform tends to follow suit toward whatever the dominant engine supports.
629cbfde7a723305: The European Space Agency's Hera probe has revealed a stadium-sized crater on Dimorphos, the asteroid NASA struck with its DART spacecraft in 2022.

The Double Asteroid Redirection Test was deliberately crashed into the asteroid on September 26, 2022. The original plan called for a European spacecraft – Asteroid Impact Mission (AIM) – to launch first and observe the before and after effects of DART. AIM was canceled, and the Hera mission launched in 2024.

DART was a success. Scientists were able to determine that the impact had indeed changed the orbit of Dimorphos. The question was what else had happened to the asteroid. Scientists spotted ejecta and debris following the DART impact, but the close-up observations by Hera have revealed the full extent of the collision.

Hera principal investigator Patrick Michel, Director of Research at CNRS / Observatoire de la Côte d'Azur, said: "Scientists debated whether Dimorphos had sustained an impact crater, changed its shape or stayed the same.

"Much to our surprise the answer turns out to be all three at once! The face struck by DART has been flattened into an impact crater the size of a sports stadium, which extends across the asteroid's entire width."
Scientists also noted that the asteroid is now tumbling in its orbit.

Hera is surveying the 151-meter-wide Dimorphos and its larger companion, the 730-meter-wide Didymos, from about 25 to 30 km away. It moves around the pair at roughly 12 cm/s, using thruster firings to trace rectangular paths rather than conventional circular orbits.

The plan is to approach closer, to about 13 km, to get higher-resolution snaps. A complicating factor is the discovery that hundreds of orbiting boulders surround the asteroids. Michael Kueppers, ESA's Hera mission scientist, said: "The team will have to take account of these objects in the coming weeks as the mission moves in closer."

Hera will deploy two CubeSats, Juventas and Milani, in early 2027. The Italian-led Milani will study surface composition and surrounding dust, while the Luxembourg-led Juventas will use radar to probe Dimorphos's interior before attempting a landing.

Scientists also want to measure Dimorphos's mass. Combined with the observed change in its orbit, that will help them assess how effectively DART transferred momentum to the asteroid and improve predictions for future deflection attempts.

Hera mission manager Ian Carnelli said: "NASA's DART mission demonstrated that we can change an asteroid's orbit. Hera is now revealing what happened to the asteroid itself. By combining these two missions, humanity is taking a decisive step towards making asteroid deflection a reliable tool for protecting our planet." ®
d1dc33707462799c: NEW DELHI: An advertisement for cardamom is at the centre of a legal spat between a Bollywood actor and India's most prominent food commissioner, with a court ruling set to shape how far companies can go in indirectly advertising brands whose promotion is restricted.

India restricts advertising for liquor and tobacco but officials have for years also frowned upon the use of indirect means, called surrogate advertising, by companies in such sectors promoting their brands in the guise of sodas, water or glassware.

While companies say these are genuine businesses in their own right whose advertising cannot be curbed, health officials say the advertisements are aimed at generating recall of the parent brand whose publicity is restricted.
Since 2024, India has been trying to finalise stringent guidelines to prohibit such advertisements outright.

In the case involving Bollywood stars, actor Ajay Devgn has sued the food authority of Maharashtra state, arguing he has been wrongly told to stop appearing in advertisements for Vimal cardamom packs, according to a non-public court filing dated Oct 15 reviewed by Reuters.

The state, whose food safety commissioner Tukaram Mundhe has become a national sensation for his aggressive stance on public health, asked Bollywood stars Devgn, Shah Rukh Khan and Tiger Shroff in August to stop appearing in advertisements promoting Vimal cardamom, arguing the brand is mostly known for its betel nut mix, or pan masala, which is banned in the state.
The spat in the High Court in Mumbai could set a precedent, New Delhi-based lawyer Anuj Tiwari said.
"The case will test both the fairness of the department's process before it imposes restrictions... and the parameters for deciding what counts as indirect advertising," he said.
In the advertisement available on Vimal Cardamom's YouTube page and posted two years ago, the Bollywood stars are seen celebrating, throwing saffron at each other after Devgn consumes the product.
The Hindi-language advertisement has 107 million views, while clips dubbed in other Indian languages have garnered millions more.
Devgn in his filing argues cardamom has not been prohibited in the state and "there is no bar in endorsing a product which is not prohibited."
Devgn did not respond to Reuters queries.

Mundhe told Reuters the state believes the advertisements are against public health interests, and the state is separately reviewing responses submitted by Khan and Shroff, although Reuters could not ascertain details of their submissions.

Dushyant Mahant, a lawyer for PB Agro, which holds the licence to make Vimal cardamom and pan masala, told Reuters the allegations were futile as the company does not promote Vimal in Maharashtra and only advertises the product via nationally televised broadcasts that cannot be restricted geographically.
Industry estimates show India's pan masala market was worth around US$5 billion last year.
Health experts say the product is a leading cause of oral fibrosis that often progresses to oral cancer.
While Maharashtra bans it, Vimal's tobacco-free pan masala sachets in other states cost around five rupees (5.4 US cents).
But they are often consumed with chewing tobacco, sold at kiosks as "twin packs" — a pan masala sachet alongside a tiny pouch of unbranded tobacco.

483f64d5371ececf: Ukraine has been executing a series of successful strikes against Russian assets around the world. Ukrainian forces disabled a Russian cargo vessel off the coast of Finland, and sunk a Russian corvette, the Merkury, along with damaging another cargo vessel, in Libyan waters. These attacks, in the aftermath of Ukraine’s severe damage to the Kerch Strait Bridge in Russian-occupied Crimea, have created hope among Ukraine’s allies. The year 2026 hasn’t advanced Ukraine’s goal of ending the war. A stagnant battlefront, increased Russian aerial attacks and a recalcitrant American president have increased the burdens on Ukraine’s government and its people. Russia hasn’t had a good year either. More than 400,000 Russians have been killed in the war — and potentially as many as 700,000. For Ukraine to have any chance of winning, it must increase the pressure on Russian leader Vladimir Putin’s government. Making Russian assets vulnerable globally is one way to do it. The international dimension Since its outset, the Russia-Ukraine conflict has had an international dimension. Ukraine’s allies, both prior to and after Russia’s full-fledged invasion in 2022, rushed supplies to Ukraine in its moment of need. Providing aid to Ukraine has continued for the past four years, despite disruptions caused by United States President Donald Trump’s involvement in the negotiation process. The supplies provided by Ukraine’s allies are critical to its success. While the fighting is conducted by the Ukrainian people and Ukraine has increased domestic arms production, outside supplies are crucial in a number of areas — notably, air defence. Equally important is the economic aid Ukraine’s allies have and continue to provide the country. Given the size differential between Russia and Ukraine and how hard the war has hit the Ukrainian economy, economic aid allows Ukraine to provide basic services to its citizens. Initially, Russia did not court outside support to the same extent as Ukraine, as it believed it would achieve a rapid victory over its adversary. Once the reality of the conflict became clear, Russia turned to the international community for support. That support has taken many forms. Iran and North Korea have been among Russia’s top supporters, providing drones and soldiers. Other countries, most notably China, have provided an economic lifeline to Russia, allowing it access to their markets in an effort to stave off the worst impacts of the economic sanctions Ukraine’s allies have imposed on the Russians. Countries in Central Asia and the Middle East have also served Russia as important intermediaries for acquiring sanctioned materials. Targeting support In a conflict that is increasingly defined by attrition, it’s been necessary for both Ukraine and Russia to rally their allies. The demands of industrialized warfare and the production of necessary armaments means neither country can produce what’s needed on their own. Because both sides are receiving critical support in this industrialized conflict, the war has reached an equilibrium. In their current states, neither side is likely to achieve a decisive breakthrough to rapidly end the fighting. For both Ukraine and Russia, that means targeting their adversary’s international allies is necessary to win the conflict. The least risky form of targeting enemy support, and among the most important, is by constructing narratives while delegitimizing those of your opponent. Ukraine has focused on Russia’s aggression and its violation of international norms and laws. The focus on international law is particularly important for Ukraine given Russian accusations that the West has flouted international norms for decades; Russia uses western association with Ukraine to gain support in the Global South. Russia has put forward several narratives to justify the war, ranging from defending itself from NATO imperialist expansion to its factually questionable claims of the Ukrainian state’s genocide against ethnic Russians in Ukraine. Russia had some early successes from these narratives, making political gains in Africa and earning support among far-right European parties. Narrative campaigns, however, typically unfold over a long time frame. As both Ukraine and Russia seek immediate ways to boost morale and undermine their adversary, direct military operations abroad have become all the more significant. Read more: Volodymyr Zelenskyy’s removal of two top defence officials highlights the role of morale in long wars Attacking the secure ‘rear’ In military terms, the rear is the area furthest from the enemy and ideally secure from military threat. For both Ukraine and Russia, this area has been other countries. While Russia and Ukraine cannot attack the assets of other countries directly, they can and do engage in espionage against other countries. For Russia, these efforts have focused on destabilizing Europe using drones and other assets via attacks that that are easily deniable. Russia also seeks to create pressure through violating European air space. The more Russia destabilizes Europe, Ukraine’s primary ally, the better its chances in the conflict. For Ukraine, Russia’s aspirations to be a so-called Great Power mean its network is global — so Ukrainian special operation forces and intelligence agencies strike at Russian assets abroad where possible. These range from attacks in nearby areas, like the Baltics, to Africa and beyond. Read more: Putin wanted to make Russia great again. Instead, Ukraine is the new rising power in Europe While news agencies view this development as widening the conflict, and the United Nations may wish to prevent the conflict from going global, the reality is it’s been a global conflict since before 2022. The strikes in Libya and the Baltic, and Ukrainian leader Volodymyr Zelenskyy immediate acknowledgement of Ukraine’s role, is just making it public. a1a9de6fe232eb4d: Microsoft's November security updates can break authentication in some third-party applications and devices following changes to NTLM message signing.
Affected systems include authentication proxy servers, single sign-on (SSO) products, and application packaging tools, the company's support notice says.

The failures stem from products that claim to supply required information during NTLM authentication but return incomplete or empty data, Microsoft said: "An affected device might set the NTLMSSP_NEGOTIATE_TARGET_INFO flag in its CHALLENGE_MESSAGE but provide an empty or incomplete TargetInfo field."

Administrators can use the notice's network trace and event log examples to identify affected products. For confirmed cases, the temporary workaround is to set the ClientAllowUnsignedNtlm Registry value to 1 on affected clients. This stops the client offering signing, backing out the new default rather than fixing the incompatible product. The recommended long-term options are a vendor update or Kerberos authentication, where supported.
The value sits under HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Lsa\MSV1_0 and defaults to 0, enabling clients to offer signing on non-anonymous connections.

The NTLM changes arrived in the November 10 update as phase 1 in a 2-phase process. In phase 1, "Windows client devices begin offering NTLM signing on all connections by default. Servers accept both signed and unsigned clients. Auditing events identify clients not using signing."
Phase 2, scheduled for May 2027, will make Windows servers require NTLM signing by default. "Clients that do not offer signing will be rejected by secure servers," Microsoft stated.
Ominously, Microsoft warned that it "might remove the registry keys at a future date," so the company is not kidding about the temporary workaround thing.

The additional protections were added to address CVE-2026-118737, a vulnerability in which "improper verification of cryptographic signature in Windows Remote Procedure Call Runtime allows an unauthorized attacker to execute code over a network."

NTLM is on Microsoft's hit list, having joined the Deprecated Features list in 2024. It dates back to the era of Windows NT, and Microsoft has made clear that it wants customers to move to Kerberos, which became the default in 2000. Even so, NTLM lingers on.

Deprecation doesn't remove Microsoft's obligation to secure NTLM while it remains in supported Windows releases. For administrators, though, the immediate task is identifying incompatible products before temporary exceptions give way to stricter enforcement. ®

2a99f168595cd5f3: In May 2025, my colleague David Rotman wrote a feature story describing how AI could keep us dependent on natural gas. Just 18 months later, I’ve lost count of how many times he’s already been proved right.

Sure, it’s technically possible to meet the world’s rising electricity demand with other power sources, including renewables like wind and solar supported by batteries. But the reality in the US so far is that the data center boom is helping to fuel a massive natural-gas resurgence.

Just one example: Plans for the Meta data center in Louisiana that David focused on in his story have expanded, and its power needs have too. The local utility went from three planned natural-gas plants to 10. And as I wrote in a new story this week, data center developers are now looking beyond the grid and planning to build their own off-grid gas power plants. How did we get here?

If you want to understand the future of the grid, one way to do it is by looking at interconnection queues—lists of power plants that have requested a connection to the system. In recent years these queues have been dominated by renewables like wind and solar power, which are generally the cheapest way to build new energy capacity today.

But there’s been a shift in some places, particularly for PJM, the country’s largest power grid operator, which covers parts of 13 states in an area stretching from Illinois to Washington, DC. PJM has seen a major uptick in natural-gas proposals. In August, the operator announced that it had accepted proposals for 715 total projects with a capacity of over 200 gigawatts to join its queue. Nearly half that total capacity represented natural-gas plants.

If all the projects in the queue were built, it would increase the fossil-fuel share on PJM’s grid from 61% to 67%, according to an analysis by Kevin Kircher, an energy modeler and assistant professor of mechanical engineering at Purdue.

PJM’s queue is reflective of a bigger trend across the US. Natural gas is already the single biggest source of electricity in the country, and it has basically become the default to meet exploding power demand.

This AI-driven rush is already affecting greenhouse-gas emissions for tech companies. Meta’s emissions are up 45% over last year’s, according to the company’s recently released 2026 Sustainability Report. That’s even higher than the jumps from fellow hyperscalers Google (18%), Amazon (16%), and Microsoft (25%). The company is also “reevaluating” its 2030 goal to reach net-zero emissions, according to the report, though there aren’t details about how or when it might reach a decision there.

And there’s another tidbit in that Meta report worth noting: The company said that when the grid can’t deliver power “on the necessary timeline,” it will look to other methods, including building its own on-site power generation.

This fits into a related and growing trend that I’ve been tracking recently: Data center developers are looking to bypass long wait times to hook up to the grid by building their own power plants instead.

It’s not new for large industrial facilities to supply their own power. Chemical plants often have natural-gas infrastructure on-site to generate electricity and heat, for example (though they’re generally connected to the grid as well). Mining operations are often remote, requiring an off-grid power source.

But the desire to come online quickly means there could be a massive boom in off-grid power plants for data centers. Over 100 such facilities have been proposed in the US, with a total capacity of 115 gigawatts (that’s more than double the entire peak power demand of California). The vast majority of these sites have been proposed since the beginning of 2025.

There are alternative ways to help meet growing electricity demand: Wind and solar are inexpensive options, and pairing them with batteries could improve their reliability, for example. I’ve also written before about demand flexibility—efforts to limit power drawn from the grid when demand is high.
Right now, though, the evidence continues to stack up that the AI boom in the US is basically synonymous with a natural-gas boom.
This article is from The Spark, MIT Technology Review’s weekly climate newsletter. To receive it in your inbox every Wednesday, sign up here.
71a6c1e46213efad: LONDON: Former England footballer Raheem Sterling was spared jail for dangerous driving on Wednesday after a judge acknowledged nitrous oxide had become a "maladapative coping mechanism" during a tough period in his career.

The 31-year-old was given a 12-month prison sentence, suspended for 18 months, at Basingstoke Magistrates' Court.

The forward, currently without a club, pleaded guilty in September to driving dangerously.
He also admitted possession of six nitrous oxide canisters for wrongful inhalation and failing to provide a specimen.
District judge Kirsty Allman acknowledged in her sentencing remarks that nitrous oxide became a "maladaptive coping mechanism during a difficult period in your career."
"Importantly, shortly after your arrest and entirely voluntarily, you engaged with addiction services," she said.
Nitrous oxide, also known as laughing gas, is legally sold for catering, medical and industrial purposes but is frequently used as a recreational drug, often inhaled using a balloon.
Allman said "numerous members of the public" had contacted police because of Sterling's dangerous driving.

"The driving involved obviously highly dangerous manoeuvres, you repeatedly drifted across lanes, undertook vehicles, made abrupt lane changes, caused motorists to brake heavily and came close to colliding with the central reservation," she added.
"The driving was significantly impaired by the consumption of drugs."
Allman said she attached "substantial weight" to Sterling's personal mitigation, including his charitable work, referring to his "positively exemplary" character.
"You enjoyed a highly successful professional football career and were widely regarded as a role model for many young people through your achievements and public profile," she said.
Sterling won 82 England caps, the last of which came at the 2022 World Cup in Qatar.
The winger made his senior debut at Liverpool before joining City in 2015, winning four Premier League titles.
He left for Chelsea in 2022 but subsequently fell out of favour and spent the 2024/25 season on loan at Arsenal.
Sterling joined Feyenoord on a short-term deal in February, playing eight times in the Eredivisie, but left at the end of the season.

1598cb54bc1efa72: The US Treasury's Financial Crimes Enforcement Network (FinCEN) has taken some systems offline following unauthorized access, disrupting regulatory filings for financial institutions.

An alert has gone up on FinCEN's Bank Secrecy Act E-Filing website, as shown in this archived copy, informing those who need to submit reports that they might not be able to while the agency deals with the situation. FinCEN not only enforces compliance with the Bank Secrecy Act and associated regulations but also collects and analyzes financial intelligence for sharing with other US agencies and foreign government partners.
In other words, it has some juicy info in its databases.

“FinCEN is investigating a cybersecurity incident that resulted in unauthorized access to a limited subset of its systems,” the alert states. “As a proactive measure, FinCEN has taken some systems offline.”

FinCEN hasn't said which systems intruders accessed, but clues in the deadline extension notice the agency posted alongside the warning suggest the disruption affects its reporting services for banks and other financial institutions required to submit reports detailing certain financial transactions and suspicious activity that may indicate money laundering or other illicit activity.

FinCEN's Secure Data Transfer Mode, one method of submitting those reports, appears to be affected, as do services companies use to submit beneficial ownership information reports and individuals use to update their FinCEN identifiers. Eligible organizations and individuals with filings or updates due from November 18 through December 29 now have until December 30 to submit them.

The Register has learned that there’s no evidence of any unauthorized access to Bank Secrecy Act data or beneficial ownership databases. That said, the investigation is ongoing - so that could change.

“Treasury is working with the Federal Bureau of Investigation, the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency, and third-party forensic examiners to determine the scope and impact of the incident,” a FinCEN official told us in an email.

Several US government agencies have experienced cybersecurity incidents in recent months, including the ATF and the FBI, and reports emerged this week that intruders had also compromised an unclassified CIA system. While US authorities have linked previous cyberespionage campaigns to Chinese or other government-backed groups, financially motivated criminal groups have also targeted federal agencies.
As the FinCEN breach is still under investigation, the agency hasn’t stated who may be involved and for what purpose. ®

bb9520d6a83b6759: KUALA LUMPUR: The United States (US) has proposed tariffs of up to 18 per cent on Malaysian goods, citing concerns that the country's industrial policies and manufacturing practices contribute to excess production that undermines US commerce.
Malaysia is among 14 economies facing proposed tariffs under Section 301 of the Trade Act with proposed headline rates ranging from 15 to 35 per cent.
The other economies include China, Singapore, Indonesia, Thailand, Vietnam, Japan, and the European Union.

In a statement on Wednesday, US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer said investigations found that certain industrial strategies adopted by trading partners had created an uneven playing field for American manufacturers.

"For decades, many of our trading partners have adopted industrial strategies built on targeting manufacturing, wage and labour suppression, financial and other support, non-market economy inputs, and other market distorting practices that tilt the trade balance in their favour while eroding America's manufacturing base," he said.

USTR's findings against Malaysia centred on four areas, namely industrial and sectoral plans to expand manufacturing and exports, preferential financing through national funding programmes, insufficient action to address excess capacity linked to imports and foreign investments from non-market economies, and inadequate labour protections.

The report identified information and communications technology (ICT) and the automotive industry as sectors of particular concern, arguing that these policies could reduce commercial opportunities for US producers and exporters in Malaysia and other markets.
Under the proposed action, tariffs of up to 18 per cent would apply to Malaysian goods, on top of existing duties where applicable, but would be subject to exemptions for certain products.
On Malaysia, USTR said the proposed tariff rate of up to 18 per cent would be net of existing Section 301 tariffs, with exemptions for certain goods.
The proposal took into account existing duties under Sections 301 and 232, ongoing consultations with Malaysia, and commitments under the US-Malaysia Agreement on Reciprocal Trade.

However, USTR also proposed considering tariffs of up to 25 per cent, net of existing Section 301 tariffs, should it find that ongoing consultations and commitments under the reciprocal trade agreement were unsatisfactory.
Greer said the proposed action was intended to address what Washington viewed as unfair trade practices and strengthen the competitiveness of American manufacturers.

"In recognition of this, since 2016, leaders ranging from Donald Trump, to Joe Biden, to Xi Jinping, to Emmanuel Macron have recognised the threat that structural excess capacity and production poses for the global economy," he said.

Meanwhile, USTR acknowledged Malaysia's position that it operates a rule-based trade regime and does not contribute to structural excess capacity, with the government maintaining that its manufacturing ecosystem was critical to global and US supply chains.
Malaysia also argued that its economic model was market-based and responsive to global demand, while its exports were complementary to, rather than in competition with, US domestic production.

The investigation into Malaysia was initiated on March 11, with USTR holding bilateral consultations with the Malaysian government on May 12, although the discussions did not resolve Washington's concerns, according to the notice.
Interested parties have until Jan 5, 2027, to submit written comments and requests to participate in the public hearings, which are scheduled to begin on Jan 25, 2027, in Washington.

0e1f90ab99b34221: WASHINGTON: Pentadbiran Presiden Amerika Syarikat (AS) Donald Trump pada Rabu mencadangkan pengenaan tarif baharu ke atas import dari 14 rakan dagang, termasuk Kesatuan Eropah (EU), China dan Malaysia, lapor Agensi Berita Jerman (dpa).

bf6f8cdf9377ad36: WASHINGTON: United States (US) President Donald Trump's administration has proposed imposing new tariffs on imports from 14 trading partners, including the European Union (EU) and China, German Press Agency (dpa) reported.

"For decades, many of our trading partners have adopted industrial strategies built on targeting manufacturing, wage and labour suppression, financial and other support, non-market economy inputs, and other market distorting practices that tilt the trade balance in their favour while eroding America's manufacturing base," Greer was quoted as saying in a statement.
Trump has imposed sweeping tariffs on the country's key trading partners since taking office in January 2025, arguing that the measures would boost US manufacturing and protect jobs.

30a7ad140b739235: WASHINGTON: US gross domestic product (GDP) growth in the third quarter (Q3) was revised strongly upwards on Wednesday, with the commerce department citing strong investment and consumer spending, as the US Federal Reserve's (Fed) preferred inflation gauge hit a three-year high in October.

US GDP growth in Q3 this year was estimated at 4.3% at an annualised rate, the department's Bureau of Economic Analysis (BEA) said, a rise of 0.9 percentage points from the previous estimate and much higher than market expectations.

"Compared to the second quarter, the acceleration in real GDP in Q3 primarily reflected an acceleration in investment and an upturn in government spending that were partly offset by a downturn in exports," the BEA said in a statement.

The US economy has shown resilient growth in recent months despite facing significant headwinds, including from president Donald Trump's chaotic tariff policies and his war on Iran, which has driven up energy prices.

Also on Wednesday, the Fed's preferred inflation gauge came in at a three-year high in October, according to BEA data, with a rise in energy prices accompanied by an increase in non-durable goods inflation.
The Personal Consumption Expenditures (PCE) Price Index rose by 3.8% year-on-year in October, the data showed, matching a three-year high set in May.
The Fed has a long-term 2% target for PCE inflation, one that it has missed for almost six years.
In September, the Fed raised interest rates for the first time in three years in order to combat the persistent price increases, which have battered US households and businesses.
The Fed's Open Market Committee (FOMC) held rates steady at its last meeting in October, but with inflation continuing to run hot, it is likely to raise rates at its next confab in December.
The years of above-target inflation since the pandemic have hit US households hard, with current price levels more than 30 percent higher than in 2020, as per the official Consumer Price Index.
Affordability was a key issue in this month's midterm elections, which saw Trump's Republican Party swept out of power in both houses of Congress by their rival Democrats.
The price increases have been driven by Trump's tariffs, energy price increases due to the war on Iran and a massive investment boom in AI technology driving up demand for some goods.
Trump has defended his economic performance by pointing to data like GDP growth, which has been robust despite the headwinds, mainly on the back of the AI boom.
Economists warn that while consumer spending has remained strong, despite the high prices, there is a growing divide between lower- and higher-income households in the US.
Heather Long, chief economist at Navy Federal Credit Union, said the fresh inflation data pointed to a likely rate hike in December, and possibly another a month later.
"America's inflation problem is bigger than an energy shock," she said. "The Fed has to act in December and likely January," she added.
She pointed out that while consumer spending did increase in absolute terms in October, it was flat once adjusted for inflation.

Ryan Sweet, chief global economist at Oxford Economics, said the strong GDP data would give Fed policymakers room to breathe when it comes to further rate hikes, which tend to cool economic activity as they tackle inflation.
"The tightening in financial market conditions, if sustained, will not have a noticeable impact on growth until the second half of next year," he said.
31290a44cad9440c: THERE are few things more infuriating than encountering inconsiderate and outrageous behaviour on the road.
A survey of 2,700 Malaysian respondents by Cilisos found that changing lanes without signalling, cutting into queues and hogging fast lanes were among the driving habits that annoyed motorists most.

Other pet peeves include double-parking without leaving a contact number, using a mobile phone while driving, misusing emergency lanes and refusing to give way. Such offenders may be cursed at or subjected to angry stares.
But do these offenders deserve to be attacked with a parang or meat cleaver, or punched by furious motorists in a fit of road rage? Certainly not. The consequences can be tragic.
An estimated 20 per cent of drivers fall into the high-anger category, exhibiting aggressive behaviour that can range from verbal abuse to physical violence.

Apart from perceived slights by other motorists, common triggers include traffic congestion, aggressive driving, poor road design, sudden lane changes and inconsistent speed limits. Poor traffic enforcement and everyday stress can also contribute to motorists' frustration.

Even the mild-mannered can turn aggressive behind the wheel. Psychological research suggests that the relative isolation of being inside a vehicle can make some drivers more reactive to perceived threats and provocations.
Few road rage incidents have been as deadly as the 2019 altercation at the Sungai Besi toll plaza.
Following a minor collision, motorist Syed Muhammad Danial Syed Shakir was struck by a car driven by Yew Wei Liang and later died. Yew was subsequently convicted of culpable homicide.
In December last year, the Federal Court reduced his prison sentence to 12 years.

More recently, a 62-year-old man was allegedly punched, elbowed and kicked following a collision involving his wife's car in Pasir Panjang, Terengganu, on Nov 23. Police arrested three men, aged between 39 and 44, who were remanded for four days on Nov 25 to assist investigations.
There are, however, ways to de-escalate such situations.
Above all, treat aggressive drivers as a hazard to avoid rather than a challenge. Never leave your vehicle during a confrontation.

Simple measures can help reduce the risk of road rage. Leave home before peak hours, signal clearly and well before changing lanes, and offer a brief hand wave or flash of your hazard lights as a courtesy.
Small courtesies can defuse tension. Avoid honking, flashing your headlights, making offensive gestures or glaring at drivers.

Consider installing front and rear dashcams to record incidents and provide evidence in the event of confrontations. If another driver is tailgating or braking suddenly, remain calm and allow the vehicle to pass when it is safe to do so. Change lanes only when conditions permit.
If an aggressive driver harasses you, head for the nearest police station or a well-lit, populated location such as a busy petrol station or highway rest area.
Call 999 if you are threatened or believe you are in immediate danger.

0aac787b287f80e0: INVESTORS were euphoric over Jensen Huang's return as chief executive officer of AI giant Nvidia on Monday.
But the extraordinary turn of events raises more questions than answers, particularly about the longer-term implications for Wall Street and the United States "free market".

Huang's return after only 11 days, which President Donald Trump said would not have happened without his personal intervention, calls into question US corporate ethics, governance, trust and accountability, not to mention the supposed separation between Washington and Wall Street.

Huang returned after he resigned amid allegations of multiple extramarital affairs with subordinates and a suspected Chinese spy whose former employer, Singapore-based Mega-speed, was just blacklisted by the US government.
Only last week, Nvidia chairman Harvey Jones said the board would not reinstate Huang.
It's no surprise that the Trump administration sees Nvidia, and the AI financing solar system that revolves around it, as too big to fail.
Nvidia's plunging share price had wiped trillions of dollars from the US stock market, and the rout was threatening to snowball.
Trump was on record saying he wanted Huang back. Investors clearly agreed.
The Nasdaq leaped seven per cent after the announcement on Monday, the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index jumped 14 per cent, and Nvidia rocketed more than 30 per cent.
But Huang's sudden return is jaw-dropping.

Huang and Nvidia still face multiple investigations from US regulators, authorities and Congress into a wide range of issues, including the possible diversion of AI chips to China, suspected Chinese spying, accounting and financing questions, and antitrust concerns.
The White House's muddled approach also rings alarm bells.

On Nov 15, Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent told Sunday Morning Futures on Fox News that Nvidia was being looked into for a "culture of non-compliance" and needed to look "outside the company" for Huang's replacement.
A week later, when pressed on his previous comment, he told CBS's Face the Nation, "Well, Jensen is on the outside now."
Whether the White House's role in this saga is bullish or bearish depends on how you view the government's growing influence on private enterprises.
This isn't the Trump administration's first foray into the private sector.
It has bought a stake in chipmaker Intel, holds a golden share in US Steel, and has secured up to 15 per cent of revenue from certain chip sales made by Nvidia and Advanced Micro Devices in China.
But Huang's return is on another level.

Many investors may be shocked by what appears to be brazen political interference in one of the country's most important companies, and critics will say billionaire tech "gurus" are playing by a different set of rules than the rest of the country.
Or, no rules at all. How can this reflect "free and fair" markets?

Yet to others, Trump's intervention is akin to former European Central Bank president Mario Draghi's pledge at the height of the euro zone debt crisis in 2012 to do "whatever it takes" to save the euro.
The US government has signalled it will essentially do whatever it takes to backstop the tech industry and ensure the US beats China in the global AI arms race.
That, of course, calls into question the notion of efficient markets and the very definition of a risk asset, and raises the issue of "moral hazard".
Markets may have cheered the return of the 'outsider' but investors should be careful what they wish for. If the White House can help install someone as CEO, it can presumably remove them as well.

"Should we start pricing political risk premium into stocks seen as sensitive to the US government's interests?" says Shivaram Rajgopal, professor of accounting and auditing at Columbia Business School.

If share prices move more on shifts in political influence than on changes in corporate earnings, investors may have to fundamentally revise their investment principles and strategies for this new era.
Trump's unorthodox and often controversial policies have rewritten large parts of the rule book on which the global economic order of the last several decades has been based.
Maybe the Nvidia move is just the latest chapter, and investors will have to get used to more government involvement in markets, whether they like it or not.
The writer is from Reuters

9c61ca4894568f78: PETALING JAYA: Imported products sold through e-commerce platforms must meet the same quality and safety standards as locally made goods before they can be marketed in Malaysia, says investment, trade and industry minister Johari Ghani.

Johari said discussions had been held with domestic trade and cost of living minister Armizan Mohd Ali and the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission to identify ways to regulate e-commerce platforms, Harian Metro reported.

“People pay for these products, but there are no standards. They are already damaged after just two or three months of use.
“Although they may initially seem to offer value for money, the reality is that they do not last,” he told a press conference on the sidelines of a Sirim event in Kuala Lumpur today.
He said the MCMC would consider action against platforms that failed to comply with the quality standards.

“This is why their prices are significantly lower,” he said.
He said the government would continue to encourage online shopping while ensuring all products sold to consumers met the required standards.
e44cc660cf435066: THE collapse of COP31 talks in Turkiye on Sunday without a political agreement left exhausted negotiators questioning the future of a process that for three decades has led the global fight against climate change.

For the small, vulnerable countries most exposed to rising sea levels and the increasingly extreme weather scientists link to rising carbon emissions, annual United Nations conferences are their chance to draw the world's attention to their plight and seek financial help.
But the failure of the Turkish talks, which follows on from weak outcomes at other COPs in recent years, lays bare the need for change.
Andres Martin Garrido Sanchez, director of environment in Peru's Foreign Affairs Ministry, said "the credibility of the process" was at stake".
"This system needs in-depth reforms," he said.
Simon Stiell, the UN climate chief representing the UN convention that underpins international climate talks, said the consensus-based system can still function, but work was needed.

"I have taken steps in engaging external knowledge leaders in advising on areas of potential reform. That is something I will be championing with considerable effort as we leave here," he said as the talks ended.

Two stand-out victories for UN climate diplomacy were the 1997 Kyoto Protocol, when the world for the first time agreed on legally binding targets to curb climate emissions and the 2015 Paris agreement, which established an aspiration to limit global warming to no more than 1.5°Celsius.
A major difference in Paris compared with Antalya was that the US was still engaged in the climate process in 2015.

The Antalya talks, the first since a UN report saying the world was set to breach the 1.5°C threshold that can prevent the worst consequences of warming, marked the second climate conference since US President Donald Trump withdrew from the UN climate process.
China, the world's biggest carbon emitter, but also a major part of the solution as a provider of low-carbon technology, has attended the talks but sought to be low profile.
James Fletcher, who led the CARICOM group of Caribbean nations in Antalya, cited the lack of a major power backing a positive outcome as a big issue.
"There isn't that one party that has sufficient gravitas that can get parties that may be far apart to come together," he said.
Delegates said, however, the need for a multilateral deal to direct the shift towards renewable energy has become less necessary as renewable energy becomes economically compelling.

China's clean energy exports last year alone, for example, will help the Global South avoid 257 million metric tonnes of carbon dioxide emissions per year once deployed — an amount equal to the emissions of France, according to analysis by Lauri Myllyvirta, co-founder of the ​Helsinki-based Centre for Research on Energy and Clean Air.
The business world as a result is less dependent on COPs to guide investment decisions.
"It used to be that you'd worry about how these (COP) decisions might affect the investment signal," said Chris Dodwell, co-head of the sustainability centre at Impax Asset Management.
"I don't think they really have that impact anymore…. economics have taken over and are driving the transition."
And bad as the absence of a deal was, some saw a hint of the positive in the wider refusal to accept a weak deal.
The determination of big oil producers to block language on fossil fuel, arguably reflected the scale of progress that has been achieved.

Like-minded governments, meanwhile, have focused on smaller groups to get things done. They have formed alliances to push together for faster emissions cuts and to rally finance, forestry initiatives, and efficiency programmes.
Such forums include the Conference on Transitioning Away from Fossil Fuels, or TAFF, the Green Grids Initiative, the Global Methane Pledge and the Beyond Oil and Gas Alliance.

"There is growing interest in how can we work together to move, not through consensus, but through a coalition of people that are willing to work together," said Maina Talia, climate minister of Tuvalu, which will next year host TAFF.
The writers are from Reuters

959613d6f36ee6aa: KUALA LUMPUR: A total of 2,296 local companies have received assistance through the government's export promotion programmes as of August, generating RM29.89 billion in actual and potential export sales.

83211bcc1b327541: NASA has settled key design choices for its planned nuclear-fission-powered spacecraft, Space Reactor-1 (SR-1) Freedom, following a mission review in October.

Targeting launch in late 2028, SR-1 would be the first fission-powered spacecraft to travel beyond Earth orbit. It is designed to demonstrate nuclear electric propulsion and deliver a capsule carrying three helicopters to Mars.

There have been some changes since NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman showed off the concept [PDF] at the agency's Ignition event in March. Improved shielding and spacecraft design will allow a shorter boom between the reactor and the spacecraft's main body, protecting its electronics and the SkyFall payload. The shorter boom will, according to NASA, "reduce weight, simplify assembly, and help streamline the spacecraft’s design."
The revised design also includes larger X-band antenna dishes to transmit data to Earth.
Decisions are still pending on how many radiator panels the vehicle needs, the output power levels of the nuclear power module, and how long the reactor will operate.

Currently, the mission calls for the spacecraft to start its reactor once it has left Earth orbit and gradually ramp up power. After a period during which performance data will be sent back to Earth, the reactor will be shut down until after the SkyFall capsule, containing a trio of Mars Ingenuity-class helicopters, is delivered to Martian orbit.
Solar arrays will power the spacecraft during its cruise to Mars. The fission reactor will then be reactivated to let engineers collect more data on its performance in deep space.
NASA also awarded a $39.3 million contract to Johns Hopkins University's Applied Physics Laboratory to develop the heat rejection system for the nuclear power module.
"Further maturation of the spacecraft plans will focus on reducing risk, simplifying the design, and staying on schedule," the agency said.
The latter part regarding the schedule is certainly a challenge. Meeting the late-2028 launch target leaves roughly two years to finish designing, building, and testing the spacecraft.

ESA is also targeting late 2028 for its long-delayed Rosalind Franklin rover. Missing the intended Mars departure opportunity could push SR-1 into a later launch window, although NASA has not specified a fallback schedule. ®

58598d7ae1e64199: DAKAR: The president of the Senegalese Football Federation (FSF), Abdoulaye Fall, on Wednesday denied Moroccan allegations that he had had "contact" with an arbitrator of the Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) who ruled that Senegal were the rightful winners of the 2025 African Cup of Nations.

The Moroccan federation (FRMF) asserted after Tuesday's ruling there had been "contact" between Fall and German arbitrator Ulrich Haas, one of the three CAS panel members, 48 hours before they decided "unanimously" to award the trophy to Senegal.
"That is absolutely false. I have never had any exchange with any member of CAS," said Fall on private television channel TFM.
"It surprised and astonished me that such accusations could even be made. I have never been in contact with anyone in connection with this procedure," he said.
In January, Senegal won a chaotic final 1-0 after extra time.

However, two months later the Confederation of African Football (CAF) sensationally overturned the result, awarding Morocco a 3-0 victory, and the title, after many Senegalese players walked off the pitch in protest at a penalty given to the hosts with the game still goalless.
The CAF Appeals Committee had justified its decision to overturn the result and declare Morocco champions based on Articles 82 and 84 of the AFCON Regulations.

Those state that if a team "refuses to play or leaves the ground before the regular end of the match without the authorisation of the referee, it shall be considered (loser) and shall be eliminated for good from the current competition".
However, the Senegal players eventually returned to the pitch and the final carried on.

The three-person CAS panel therefore considered the referee's decision to restart the final showed "the conditions for resuming the match had been met", and that articles 82 and 84 were therefore "not applicable in this case".
The Moroccan federation has the option of lodging an appeal with the Swiss Federal Supreme Court, which does not rule on the merits of the case but intervenes in procedural matters.

9aeeb16a2f0882b6: KUALA LUMPUR: Strengthening Malaysia's food security will require more than higher production, with Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim calling for longstanding weaknesses in agriculture, livestock and fisheries to be addressed.
He said businesses with strong potential should have better access to early financing, including through Agrobank, to help them expand domestic food production and build sustainable operations.

Citing Farm Fresh Bhd as an example, Anwar said the company's growth had been supported by initial capital from Khazanah Nasional Bhd, demonstrating how early assistance could help promising businesses develop and reach wider markets.

He was responding to a question from Farm Fresh group chief operating officer Azmi Zainal on how the government could protect consumers while ensuring food producers remained viable amid rising costs.

Speaking on RTM's special Di Sebalik Keputusan... Dialog Negara programme last night, Anwar said geopolitical tensions, including conflicts involving Iran, Israel and the United States, as well as the Russia-Ukraine war, had added pressure to food and agriculture industries.
Shipping costs had risen tenfold, pushing up the price of imported inputs such as phosphates transported through strategic routes, including the Strait of Hormuz.

"All countries in Asia and even in Europe are now facing political and social tensions due to rising prices of goods, partly due to national fiscal policies and partly due to the problem of rising imported goods," he said.
Anwar, who is also Finance Minister, said efforts to boost domestic production must be matched by reliable supplies of essential inputs, including fertilisers, and better marketing infrastructure.
He also warned that large government allocations would achieve little without strict oversight to prevent leakages and the entrenched practice of paying commissions.

"Governance must not be neglected, as excessive leakages of funds can lead to a situation where the problem becomes deeply systemic. When we eventually take action, the backlash is severe and the anger widespread because those involved have become accustomed to receiving commissions," he said. — BERNAMA
b2d94b6d294ae968: KUALA LUMPUR: All eligible flood victims will receive the RM1,000 compassionate cash aid, including those who do not seek shelter at temporary relief centres, Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi said.
He said the government had a mechanism to ensure that victims who chose not to evacuate to centres also receive the assistance, subject to verification.
"Some may have their own reasons for not moving to relief centres, such as staying at their children's or siblings' homes.
"We have a mechanism in place requiring them to lodge a police report to verify that they are flood victims," he told Bernama.

Zahid, who is also Central Disaster Management Committee chairman, was speaking after attending the 14th Asean Ministerial Meeting on Disaster Management (AMMDM), the 15th Conference of the Parties (COP) to the Asean Agreement on Disaster Management and Emergency Response (AADMER), and related meetings hosted by Indonesia.
He is on a five-day working visit to Indonesia and arrived in Jakarta yesterday after holding several meetings on rural development cooperation in Bali since Monday.
The aid provides RM1,000 to each eligible head of household.

On Nov 19, Zahid told the Dewan Rakyat that priority was given to flood victims staying at relief centres, while those who did not evacuate were also eligible if registered at a flood victim registration centre.
On the allocation for the aid, he said the amount would depend on current needs, but cautioned the public against abusing the assistance mechanism.
"Do not take advantage of a difficult situation. I am confident that Nadma (National Disaster Management Agency) handled this as best as possible," he said.
Apart from financial assistance, Zahid said the government was also strengthening flood preparedness, with Nadma having deployed the necessary assets to states affected by floods.
Preparations were also under way in other states at risk.
He said disaster management efforts were being coordinated through a whole-of-government approach, regardless of political differences.
"We are colour-blind when it comes to managing disasters," he said, adding that coordination was carried out through the Central Disaster Management Committee, with Nadma serving as its secretariat.

Zahid also thanked more than 580 non-governmental organisations (NGOs) involved in the current disaster management efforts and hoped that all preparations could be implemented in a more coordinated manner.

Ahead of the northeast monsoon, he had previously said that more than 100,000 personnel from various response and technical agencies were mobilised, supported by nearly 2,500 boats, more than 2,000 four-wheel-drive vehicles, over 1,100 lorries and 28 aircraft.

As of this morning, 1,181 flood victims from 333 families were still taking shelter at 10 relief centres in Selangor, Perak and Terengganu, with 819, 211 and 151 victims respectively, Bernama reported.

Sabah was also affected by floods following heavy rain since yesterday. The Sabah Disaster Management Committee said 153 residents from 42 families in three villages in the Sook district had been evacuated to a relief centre as of noon today.

2acc80c8149562c0: KUALA LUMPUR: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has backed the Ministry of Education's (MOE) proposal to teach mental health in schools to help pupils cope with stress.

Speaking on RTM's Dialog Negara programme on TV1 tonight, Anwar said religious and moral education should also help pupils put what they learn into practice.

"Religious and moral education should be central. Islamic education should make a difference too. Muslim pupils study Islam and pray together, but I agree that what they learn does not always translate into how they live," he said.

Anwar said schools needed more trained counsellors to deal with serious cases. Expanding counselling services would require substantial funding and could take time, he said, calling for greater public awareness in the meantime.

"Our responses are very compartmentalised. We need to raise awareness in the community. Parents have responsibilities, and so do teachers. If we take those responsibilities seriously and do our best, we can address some of these problems," he said.

Citing a briefing to the Cabinet, Anwar said most cases involving school pupils, including bullying, stemmed from pressures at home, such as excessive academic demands, as well as mistreatment and abuse at school.
He said the government could consider proposals from the Education and Health ministries and non-governmental organisations, but he also called for wider awareness, particularly among families.
"However busy parents are, they still have a responsibility to care for and guide their children, give them time and space, and show them affection," he said.

9cd89e83a169cbf2: KUALA LUMPUR: The US has proposed additional tariffs of up to 18% on Malaysian goods following an investigation into the country's industrial policies and manufacturing practices.
The US Trade Representative (USTR) said these policies contributed to structural excess capacity and production that Washington believes burdens or restricts US commerce.
Malaysia is among 14 economies facing the proposed tariffs under Section 301 of the Trade Act of 1974, with headline rates ranging from 15% to 35%.
The other economies include China, Singapore, Indonesia, Thailand, Vietnam, Japan and the European Union.

In a statement, US trade representative Jamieson Greer said investigations found that certain industrial strategies adopted by trading partners had created an uneven playing field for American manufacturers.

“For decades, many of our trading partners have adopted industrial strategies built on targeting manufacturing, wage and labour suppression, financial and other support, non-market economy inputs, and other market-distorting practices that tilt the trade balance in their favour while eroding America’s manufacturing base,” he said.

The USTR's findings against Malaysia centred on four areas: industrial and sectoral plans to expand manufacturing and exports; preferential financing through national funding programmes; insufficient action to address excess capacity linked to imports and foreign investments from non-market economies; and inadequate labour protections.

The report identified the information and communications technology and automotive industries as sectors of particular concern, arguing that these policies could limit commercial opportunities for US producers and exporters in Malaysia and other markets.
The proposed tariffs of up to 18% would be imposed on Malaysian goods on top of existing duties, where applicable, subject to exemptions for certain products.
The USTR said the proposed rate took into account existing duties under Sections 301 and 232, ongoing consultations with Malaysia, and commitments under the US-Malaysia Agreement on Reciprocal Trade.

However, it also proposed considering tariffs of up to 25%, net of existing Section 301 tariffs, if it found that ongoing consultations and commitments under the reciprocal trade agreement were unsatisfactory.
Greer said the proposed measures were intended to address what Washington viewed as unfair trade practices and strengthen the competitiveness of American manufacturers.

“In recognition of this, since 2016, leaders ranging from Donald Trump, to Joe Biden, to Xi Jinping, to Emmanuel Macron have recognised the threat that structural excess capacity and production poses for the global economy,” he said.

The USTR also acknowledged Malaysia's position that it operated a rule-based trade regime and did not contribute to structural excess capacity. The government maintained that its manufacturing ecosystem was critical to global and US supply chains.
Malaysia also argued that its economic model was market-based and responsive to global demand, while its exports complemented rather than competed with US domestic production.

The investigation into Malaysia was initiated on March 11, with the USTR holding bilateral consultations with the Malaysian government on May 12. However, the discussions did not resolve Washington's concerns, according to the notice.
Interested parties have until Jan 5, 2027, to submit written comments and requests to participate in public hearings scheduled to begin in Washington on Jan 25.

ac77df5d99922b78: KUALA LUMPUR: A 32-year-old Libyan student pleaded not guilty in the magistrate's court today to a charge of reckless driving that caused the death of a retired soldier on Jalan Jelatek last Saturday.
Ali Abdul Rahman Mahmoud Elmaki, a private university student, entered his plea after the charge was read out in english before magistrate Amalina Johar.

He was accused of driving a Proton Saga recklessly and dangerously along Jalan Jelatek, from Wangsa Maju towards Taman Keramat, at 1am on Nov 21, resulting in the death of 43-year-old Mohd Hairezam Omar.

The charge was framed under Section 41(1) of the Road Transport Act 1987, which carries a maximum fine of RM50,000 or imprisonment of up to 10 years upon conviction. A conviction under the section also carries an endorsement on the offender's driving licence.
Deputy Public Prosecutor Mohamad Fadhly Mohd Zamry objected to bail, citing the seriousness of the offence and the accused's status as a foreign national.
However, he said that should the court exercise its discretion to grant bail under Section 388 of the Criminal Procedure Code, the prosecution proposed RM70,000 bail with two Malaysian sureties.

"The prosecution also requests additional conditions: that the accused's passport be surrendered to the court, that he reports to the nearest police station at least once a month, and that he is prohibited from using his driving license until the conclusion of the case.
"I request that the court consider these conditions should bail be granted, given that the accused is a foreign national and poses a flight risk," he said.
Lawyer K. Ramalingam, representing the accused, requested bail of about RM10,000, saying his client was pursuing a master's degree and was scheduled to sit for examinations next month.
"The accused resides in Malaysia with his wife and has a permanent address on Jalan Ampang. He is also prepared to accept all additional conditions requested by the prosecution," he said.

The court granted bail at RM17,000 with two Malaysian sureties, subject to the accused surrendering his passport, reporting to a nearby police station once a month and having his driving licence suspended until the conclusion of the case.

5dc56aac589d0216: KUALA LUMPUR: The government will study whether to set up a fund to share the economic gains from artificial intelligence (AI) with Malaysians, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said tonight.

Anwar said he had asked the Communications and Digital ministries to study the options, including a proposal by US Senator Bernie Sanders for legislation to establish an AI fund that would pay dividends to Americans.
"I agree in principle. We can start engaging now, even before legislation is in place. For example, when we set a minimum wage, multinational companies have to comply too.

"At first, they objected, saying they came to Malaysia because wages were low. That may have been true 30 years ago. They now have to accept that living standards have risen," he said on RTM's Dialog Negara programme on TV1 tonight.
The programme was also simulcast on Bernama TV, Astro AWANI, TV3, TV AlHijrah and TVS.
Anwar said Malaysia imposed firm conditions on foreign AI investors, including requirements to provide water supply infrastructure and train Malaysians in advanced AI skills.
The Prime Minister cited what he described as a USD15 billion investment by Google.

He said the conditions included spending RM600 million on water supply infrastructure in Negeri Sembilan and providing advanced AI training for 1,000 young Malaysians, with Universiti Malaya as an example of a potential training partner.
"If the conditions are too onerous, investors may stay away. We should make clear that we welcome investment while taking firm steps to keep inequality from widening," he said.
Anwar said governments had a role in ensuring the benefits of growth were more widely shared across the economy.
The spread of AI made that more urgent because it could deepen inequality, he said.

On the impact of AI on jobs, Anwar said rapid technological change and unexpected shocks could bring challenges, including financial pressures. He said people could anticipate those problems and devise solutions.
He said government departments and the private sector should receive support to create new jobs as technology evolves.

The Dialog Negara panellists included Komuniti Pejuang Hartanah founder Datuk Ahyat Ishak, KRA group strategy director Amir Fareed Rahim, medical officer and social media influencer Dr Malar Santhi Santherasegapan, and entrepreneur and digital content creator Adam Shamil.

Also on the panel were PlusVibes Group founder and chief executive Dr Madiha Fuad, Farm Fresh Berhad group chief operating officer Azmi Zainal, independent preacher Izzhar Nazri, Architects of Diversity (AOD) Malaysia founder Jason Wee, and Universiti Teknologi MARA (UiTM) Student Representative Council president Mohamad Adib Hazim Mohamad Razali. -- BERNAMA

46a7a564b7c2a869: PETALING JAYA: Polis tidak menjumpai sebarang arahan dan kebenaran daripada mana-mana pihak berkuasa kerajaan berhubung surat dihantar kepada Agensi Perisikan Pusat (CIA) Amerika Syarikat (AS) bagi memohon sokongan untuk pentadbiran Najib Razak menjelang PRU14, kata Menteri Dalam Negeri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail.

Dalam jawapan bertulis di Parlimen kepada Pang Hok Liong (PH-Labis), Saifuddin berkata Jabatan Peguam Negara memutuskan pada 25 Nov 2025, tepat setahun lalu, untuk tidak mengambil tindakan lanjut terhadap kes itu.

Pang bertanya sama ada siasatan polis mendapati surat oleh bekas ketua pengarah Organisasi Perisikan Luar Malaysia (MEIO) itu dihantar dengan kebenaran atau arahan mana-mana pihak berkuasa kerajaan dan apakah keputusan siasatan tersebut.
Saifuddin berkata polis menyiasat kes itu mengikut Akta Rahsia Rasmi 1972, Seksyen 203A Kanun Keseksaan dan Seksyen 233 Akta Komunikasi dan Multimedia 1998.
"Siasatan yang lengkap dijalankan dan mendapati tidak menjumpai sebarang arahan dan kebenaran daripada pihak berkuasa kerajaan dalam isu ini.
"Kertas siasatan dirujuk kepada Jabatan Peguam Negara (AGC) pada 18 Dis 2023 dan setelah meneliti hasil siasatan, AGC pada 25 Nov 2025 memutuskan tiada tindakan lanjut atas siasatan ini," katanya.
Jawapan itu tidak menyatakan sama ada mana-mana individu telah disoal siasat atau dikenal pasti, selain tidak menjelaskan alasan di sebalik keputusan AGC.
Surat yang ditujukan kepada pengarah CIA ketika itu, Gina Haspel, muncul pada Julai 2018 ketika peralihan kerajaan selepas PRU14 pada tahun berkenaan.

Surat tiga halaman itu, yang ditandatangani oleh Ketua Pengarah MEIO ketika itu, Hasanah Abdul Hamid, memohon sokongan AS terhadap pentadbiran Najib walaupun Barisan Nasional (BN) hanya memperoleh majoriti mudah atau menang dengan satu kerusi dalam PRU 2018.

Surat itu, antara lain, menggambarkan Najib yang ketika itu perdana menteri sebagai sahabat AS, berbanding Dr Mahathir Mohamad yang ketika itu pengerusi Pakatan Harapan (PH) dan digambarkan sebagai 'anti-Barat, anti-Semitik'.
Hasanah pernah mempertahankan dirinya daripada tuduhan khianat berhubung surat yang ditulisnya kepada Haspel, dengan berkata pertukaran surat sedemikian antara agensi perisikan adalah perkara biasa.
Najib menafikan mengetahui kewujudan surat itu atau mengarahkan Hasanah menulisnya.

d75cacdd88c456f6: KUALA LUMPUR: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has given assurance that the proposed Urban Renewal (URA) Bill would protect existing residents' rights, including those who oppose redevelopment, even as the government lowers the consent threshold from 100 per cent to between 70 and 80 per cent.
Anwar said the Bill was needed to allow run-down housing, particularly in Kuala Lumpur, to be redeveloped, and requiring every resident to agree had made it difficult for projects to proceed.
"If you require 100 per cent consent, these housing projects won't go ahead. We decided on a threshold of 70 or 80 per cent, with guarantees to protect the rights of those who disagree.

"I can't bear to see housing in such poor condition in Kuala Lumpur. Something has to be done, and we need a law with clear guarantees that protect the rights of existing residents," he said on Dialog Negara programme on TV1 tonight.
The programme was also simulcast on Bernama TV, Astro AWANI, TV3, TV AlHijrah and TVS.
Anwar said the government was developing several new sites in Kuala Lumpur and other major cities under its Madani development initiative.

He expected to launch several housing projects this December or January next year, adding that such developments typically took two to three years and that work already under way was nearing completion.
He said the new homes would be considerably more comfortable and that developers would have to meet conditions set by local authorities before any agreement was signed.
Strict enforcement was needed to reassure residents after past projects had been left unfinished for years without firm action, he said.

Anwar also rejected claims that the Bill was intended to help a particular ethnic group take control of residential areas or to serve developers' interests. He said the MADANI government remained committed to safeguarding the interests of Malays and Bumiputera.

"For the first time since independence, land in Kuala Lumpur has been designated as Malay reserve land, with 50 acres to start with. That has never happened before. We will not give in to demands from powerful investors," he said.

The Dialog Negara panellists included Komuniti Pejuang Hartanah founder Datuk Ahyat Ishak, KRA group strategy director Amir Fareed Rahim, medical officer and social media influencer Dr Malar Santhi Santherasegapan, and entrepreneur and digital content creator Adam Shamil.
