3e5fea7129ca2d51: TAIPING: A 19-year-old teenager was brought before the magistrate's court today on a charge of murdering her newborn baby girl by stabbing last week.
Nurul Iman Najiha Abdullah nodded when the murder charge was read out before magistrate R. Prabakaran.
However, no plea was recorded as the case falls under the jurisdiction of the High Court.
She was accused of murdering her biological daughter in an oil palm area behind a house in Kampung Panchor, Pantai Remis, in the Larut, Matang and Selama district, between Nov 14 and 16.
The charge was framed under Section 302 of the Penal Code, which carries the death penalty or imprisonment of between 30 and 40 years.
If not sentenced to death, an offender is also liable to whipping of at least 12 strokes upon conviction.

In a separate charge, Iman Najiha and her boyfriend, Mohamad Aidil Eikmal, also 19, were jointly charged with concealing the birth of the baby girl by secretly burying her body at the same location during the same period.
They were charged under Section 318 of the Penal Code, read together with Section 34 of the same code, which provides for a maximum prison sentence of two years, or a fine, or both, upon conviction.
Aidil pleaded guilty, while Iman Najiha claimed trial.
Deputy Public Prosecutor Farihah Adilah Faizal requested bail of RM50,000 with one surety for each accused. No bail was offered for the murder charge faced by Iman Najiha.

However, National Legal Aid Foundation counsel Nurul Hanis Mohd Zaini, representing both accused, appealed for lower bail, saying this was their first offence and that they worked as an eatery assistant and construction labourer respectively.
"Iman Najiha also has mental health issues but has never sought treatment," the lawyer said.
Bail was set at RM5,000 with two sureties for each accused.
The court fixed Jan 4 for a re-mention, for Iman Najiha to appoint a lawyer and for the Social Welfare Department to submit a social report on Aidil ahead of sentencing.
On Nov 19, Perak Police Chief Datuk Mohd Alwi Zainal Abidin said a newborn baby girl had died after allegedly being stabbed by her biological mother in Pantai Remis on Nov 14.
He said preliminary investigations found that the 19-year-old had committed the act at her home before contacting her boyfriend to help bury the baby's body behind the house.

"I've already said that my directive should apply across the board. That means action must be taken even if the planned amendments take longer," he said, adding that the Higher Education Ministry was moving quickly to repeal provisions in AUKU.
Anwar said some provisions in the two laws governing UiTM students imposed tighter restrictions and should be reviewed to give students more room to express their views and think independently.
"Our Bumiputera students should be given space and freedom. Let them speak. Let them express their views. Why should we restrict how they think?" he said.

He said discipline had long been used to justify restrictions on student expression, but, in this modern era, universities should trust students to exercise their judgement and give them opportunities to develop it.

"I don't want to use the law to police students. Let's give them room. If we don't help young people develop their judgement and show confidence and trust in them, what kind of future will we have?" he said.

However, he added, students who committed criminal offences would remain subject to the relevant laws. -- BERNAMA

e4e24ac0ea4f98c1: KUALA LUMPUR: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has described corruption in the country as a systemic issue that requires the sustained commitment and firm resolve of all parties to eradicate it, including by fostering an awareness of integrity among the younger generation.
He noted that the fight against corruption is no easy task, given that the practice has become deeply entrenched within the system.
Therefore, he said the government must continue to take decisive action, without allowing the pursuit of popularity to be a primary consideration.

"Corruption in this country has become systemic. That is what I inherited. We have to stand firm and keep going, whether it's popular or not. Popularity is secondary," he said on RTM's Dialog Negara programme on TV1 tonight, which was also simulcast on RTMKlik, Bernama TV, Astro AWANI, TV3, TV AlHijrah and TVS.

Anwar said fighting corruption had proved harder than expected, making it all the more important to instil a sense of integrity from an early age, as young people could drive change and help secure Malaysia's future.
He said he had reached out to young people through various programmes, including meetings at higher education institutions, to encourage them to make integrity a guiding principle.
"We want them to hold on to their ideals. They are our hope. If we can convince Gen Z and Gen Y of the importance of integrity, our future will be more secure. That is my hope," he said.

Asked about allegations that influential people linked to corruption received preferential treatment, Anwar said the rule of law must be upheld, and the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) must be free to investigate without interference from interested parties.
He cited the case of his former senior political secretary, Datuk Seri Shamsul Iskandar Mohd Akin, who was charged in a corruption case. Anwar said he had stayed out of the investigation.

"When someone close to me is being investigated, of course I ask what it's about. He told me, and I said I wouldn't interfere. He was then charged. Has anything like that happened before? No. My Cabinet colleagues know I won't defend anyone involved in corruption," he said.
Looking ahead to 2027, Anwar said he hoped all Malaysians would carry out their responsibilities with integrity so that the country's development continued to be guided by that principle.
He said students, families and the wider community all had a part in building the country, alongside leaders and civil servants.

"Our problems are about principles and conduct. We shouldn't hate one another or see these problems through the lens of race. We have to put things right together and build on our strengths. As I've said, we have tremendous potential to raise Malaysia's standing," he said.

The Dialog Negara panellists included Komuniti Pejuang Hartanah founder Datuk Ahyat Ishak, KRA group strategy director Amir Fareed Rahim, medical officer and social media influencer Dr Malar Santhi Santherasegapan, and entrepreneur and digital content creator Adam Shamil.

The panel also included PlusVibes Group founder and chief executive Dr Madiha Fuad, Farm Fresh Berhad group chief operating officer Azmi Zainal, independent preacher Izzhar Nazri, Architects of Diversity (AOD) Malaysia founder Jason Wee, and Universiti Teknologi MARA (UiTM) Student Representative Council president Mohamad Adib Hazim Mohamad Razali. -- BERNAMA

156c769ce2529e47: KUALA LUMPUR: The government will consider introducing stricter regulations to control the entry of cheap goods through international e-commerce platforms, especially from China, said Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim.
Anwar, who is also the Minister of Finance, said the influx of foreign products affects the macro economy and directly undermines the competitiveness of local entrepreneurs.
"I agree, and I think we should introduce stricter regulations," he said on Radio Televisyen Malaysia's (RTM) special "Di Sebalik Keputusan..." Dialog Negara programme aired tonight.

The prime minister responded to Chunk & Dunk's founder, Adam Shamil, on how the government balances competition from cheap international e-commerce goods on platforms such as Pinduoduo and Temu to protect local entrepreneurs and brands.
However, Anwar said the government will not completely block or restrict these foreign platforms, but the quality and standards of the products sold must be monitored, including their halal status.

"This is why we are starting to impose some restrictions now. We will give them the opportunity to enter on the condition that local companies are involved or that they provide guarantees of quality and health. And, if it is labelled halal, it must be guaranteed as halal," he said.

Anwar said the matter was also raised with China's leaders during several visits to the country, and Chinese President Xi Jinping informed of China's readiness to increase space for Malaysian export goods.
"We do not intend to restrict, but what we want is investment and trade, not an influx of cheap goods... and this is killing smaller companies.
"So, we have agreed in the Cabinet to take several steps to curb slightly, but not completely restrict, because this goes against our (trade) policy to allow increased imports," he said.
At the same time, Anwar also reminded the people not to be mesmerised by advertisements for products whose quality has not been guaranteed.
"This is an old theory, Babylon's conspicuous consumption. Sometimes, people want to purchase unnecessary things because of extensive advertising," he said.
Anwar said the government needs to monitor advertisements, ensure product quality, and strengthen consumer education so people buy what they need and do not spend more than they earn. -- BERNAMA

4a86565e43195090: Microsoft has released a fix for a baffling bug that threw a blank window over Office applications and brought work to a standstill. The problem appeared when users launched an affected Office app, which could display an empty dialog box with no text and no buttons.
Because the dialog offered no way to close it, some users were locked out of their work entirely, unable to continue until the issue was resolved.

The good news is that there's an update to fix the problem – version 2611, build 16.0.20625.20142. The bad news is that you might not be able to launch the applications to perform the update because of that blank dialog window.

Microsoft instructs affected users to save their work, close all Office applications, and open Command Prompt as administrator. They can then force the update with: "%programfiles%\Common Files\Microsoft Shared\ClickToRun\officec2rclient.exe" /update user updatetoversion=16.0.20625.20142
The glitch affects a swathe of Microsoft 365 products – Excel, Word, Outlook, PowerPoint, Access, and OneNote.

Users reported the problem on Microsoft's forums, where volunteer moderator Stefan Blom noted that "this seems to be a common error at the moment" and suggested users try an Office repair or the more thorough Online Repair.
Online Repair reinstalls Office, however, some users reported activation and sign-in problems alongside the blank windows, which may hint at the cause. Microsoft has yet to elucidate.
Other users found that rolling back Office resolved the issue, while several reported that signing in with another application, such as Edge, fixed things.

For administrators preparing fleets of devices, a dialog that blocks first use creates another deployment headache. One user with E3 licensing reported: "We can't just hand off a staged machine without getting call[s] that our new users can't get Office to work because of the blank licensing window."
Microsoft has shared a fix for the problem, but has not stated which versions of its productivity applications were affected, nor has it explained what went wrong.
The fix is welcome. An explanation of how Office ended up blocking users with a window containing nothing at all would be welcome too. ®

ed22de253e690a12: PETALING JAYA: Police found no instruction or permission from any government authority for a letter sent to the US Central Intelligence Agency (CIA) seeking support for Najib Razak’s administration ahead of the 14th general election, says home minister Saifuddin Nasution Ismail.
In a written parliamentary reply to Pang Hok Liong (PH-Labis), Saifuddin said the Attorney General's Chambers decided on Nov 25, 2025, exactly a year ago, to take no further action on the case.

Pang had asked whether the police investigation found that the letter, sent by a former director-general of the Malaysian External Intelligence Organisation (MEIO), was written with the authority or direction of any government body, and what the outcome of the probe was.
Saifuddin said police investigated the case under the Official Secrets Act 1972, Section 203A of the Penal Code, and Section 233 of the Communications and Multimedia Act 1998.
“The investigation is complete, and it turned up no instruction or permission (was given) from government authorities.
“The investigation paper was referred to the Attorney General's Chambers on Dec 18, 2023. After reviewing it, the AGC decided on Nov 25, 2025 that there would be no further action.”
The reply did not say whether any individual was questioned or named, nor did it explain the reasons behind the AGC's decision.
The letter addressed to then CIA director Gina Haspel surfaced in July 2018 during the change of government after the 14th general election that year.

The three-page letter, signed by then MEIO director-general Hasanah Abdul Hamid, appealed for US support for Najib’s administration even if Barisan Nasional won only a simple majority or a single seat at the 2018 general election.
The letter, among others, described then prime minister Najib as a friend of the US, as opposed to the “anti-West, anti-Semite” Dr Mahathir Mohamad, who was then the Pakatan Harapan chairman.
Hasanah had defended herself against accusations of treason over the letter she wrote to Haspel, saying it was normal for intelligence agencies to exchange such letters.
Najib denied any knowledge of the letter or that he instructed Hasanah to write it.

7edbf2f828c91402: BOSTON: Nvidia's board undermined its claims of independence by reinstating CEO Jensen Huang before investigations into his conduct concluded, investors and corporate governance experts said on Monday.

"The decision is striking because the board effectively vouched for Huang's candor and fitness to lead the company before its own investigation was complete, raising doubts about whether directors had sufficient information to make an independent judgment," these people said.
Nvidia said on Monday that after talks with senior US officials, its board "is confident that Mr Huang’s reinstatement poses no national security risk".
Huang resigned on Nov 12 after reports of extramarital affairs, including one involving a suspected Chinese spy.
The abrupt U-turn, just days after the board vowed to look elsewhere for a successor, has also drawn US president Donald Trump and his administration into Nvidia’s corporate governance.
Nvidia shares closed 31.5% higher on Monday even as it was becoming clear that the chipmaker's board acted under pressure from Trump and others, and the president took credit for the change.
Nvidia faces investigations, including by the US Securities and Exchange Commission and the justice department, over issues ranging from its accounting to alleged chip smuggling.
Nvidia press representatives did not immediately respond to questions for this story.
The situation undercuts the board's standing, said New York City Comptroller Mark Levine, who helps manage retirement funds that hold some 5 million Nvidia shares.

"They told us flatly that he would not be coming back. They have done a total 180 without any explanation, or any indication that concerns about legal and other liabilities have been resolved," Levine said in a telephone interview.
"They have proven they're not independent, and that is the defining quality that we need from any board," he said.
Jan van Eck, a large Nvidia investor via the investment company bearing his name, said Huang's return likely removes uncertainty but amounts to a bet against further bad headlines.

"I had expected more of a Washington DC process, including Congressional hearings, to lengthen this determination, but I guess the Administration is willing to risk that there are no more bad facts to emerge," van Eck said in an email.
Questions of candor
In addition to saying Huang's return posed no national security risk, Nvidia's board said that after discussions, it was "satisfied with respect to Mr Huang’s candor and ability to lead Nvidia".

The company said an independent board committee is still investigating reports that Huang was targeted by a foreign intelligence effort, and said "the committee’s investigation will proceed to conclusion," with Huang's cooperation.
The board has also taken steps like creating a new chief compliance officer position.

Nada Kakabadse, a Henley Business School professor who follows corporate governance, said the statement left gaps. " 'Satisfied with his candor' is a strange phrase while the investigation into what he told the company is still open. The board has reached its verdict before the evidence is in," Kakabadse said.
"Moreover, the board has given away much of the company's room for maneuver," she said.

"It hands the board's judgment to the state. The same government that grants Nvidia's export licences now effectively vouches for its CEO. That makes the company politically dependent, and a future administration could withdraw the endorsement," she said.
Nvidia board member Harvey Jones took the title of chair only this month.
Until then, Nvidia was one of only two companies in the S&P 500 without a board chair, according to researcher Equilar.
Corporate governance experts previously had said the setup and the presence of many long-serving directors meant the board would have to show it could act independently.

Now, alongside relief at Huang's return, "there are sure to be questions about who is best placed to provide appropriate governance and oversight of key risks at the now-giant company at the centre of a critically important global AI ecosystem," said Lindsey Stewart, Morningstar director of institutional insights.
"In reappointing Huang the board left those questions unanswered," Stewart said.
Scepticism from some lawmakers
US congressional committees will interview Huang on Dec 1. Lawmakers from both parties expressed scepticism about his return and the role of the administration.
Some investors worried the political battles could overshadow Nvidia's commercial story.

"Jensen’s return is not a total shock, but it does send a troubling message about the state of corporate governance in America. Certain executives are going to be held to different standards," said James St. Aubin, CIO of Ocean Park Asset Management in California.

Harvard Law School professor Lucian Bebchuk said there was no indication the board had secured the support of Nvidia’s largest shareholders, nominally the owners of the company. (Top fund firms BlackRock and Vanguard did not comment for this story.)
Bebchuk said recent policies put in place by Trump-appointed regulators make it harder for big fund firms to weigh in on corporate governance issues.
"Even if Huang poses no national security risks in the future, his actions to date could still entangle him and the company in costly investigations," Bebchuk said.

"The board presumably feels now vindicated by the immediate stock price increase following this morning’s announcement. However, the board’s reversal of its earlier decision raises serious questions and concerns," Bebchuk said.
c7a5869b3d7038ed: JetBrains has revamped a benchmark for evaluating large language models after suspecting too many agents gamed their tasks the first time round.
The company labelled this agentic practice "reward hacking" in a post summarizing the results of its revised evaluation.

Like its predecessor, Kotlin Benchmark 2.0 is a collection of tasks that evaluates how well AI coding agents work with the Kotlin programming language, in order to help Kotlin programmers decide which agent-model configurations to use. The tasks include fixing tricky problems in Kotlin code across different domains, and making corrections to multiple files.
Dirty data

The revised benchmark now includes 30 Kotlin multi-file code problems that have not been exposed to the public in any way before. The revised test all but guarantees that the agents have not encountered this set of problems, or potential solutions, before. Another 70 tasks are based on code that resides in public repositories.

The test also blocked all network access for the open source tasks, except for what was needed to communicate with the model itself. This minimized the possibility that the agent could look for an existing answer already posted, perhaps through a patch or pull request.
A 30-minute limit was set for each task.

Overall, the agents were significantly less accurate when solving problems on codebases they had never encountered. Top resolution rates dropped rather suspiciously from 86.2 percent on tasks based on open source repositories to 60 percent on those based on closed source repositories.

Although the agents lacked network access, JetBrains boffins theorized that they might have benefited from encountering and internalizing these open source repositories during training. Only the private repositories were completely new to them.
Also curious was how a different set of models excelled at the closed source problems, compared to those models that usually did better on the open source tasks.
Leaderboard Shakeup

When restricted to closed source tasks, two dark horse models rose to the top: Gemini 3.8 Flash, via Antigravity CLI, topped the list with a 60 percent success rate, closely followed by DeepSeek V4.1 Flash (running on OpenCode) at 58.9 percent.
Of the two, the open weight DeepSeek was far cheaper (at $0.08 per task) than the closed weight Gemini ($1.74 per task), however.

In contrast, Opus 5.5 completed only 53.3 percent of the tasks at $1.21 per task, and Fable 5.1 completed only 44.4 percent of the tasks, at a luxurious $3.27 per task. Claude Code harnessed both of these models.
Claude’s lackluster completion rates on closed source tasks are somewhat sus given how both of these Anthropic models scored significantly higher on tasks using open source materials.
In fact Claude ran the table when it came to open source: Fable 5.1 topped the charts with 86.2 percent accuracy, closely followed by Opus 5.5 at 84.8 percent accuracy.
(Kotlin users will pay dearly for the extra sliver of Anthropic accuracy: The average cost of Fable completing a Kotlin cleanup task runs $2.38, while Opus could do the job for $0.68.)
Gaming the boss

One possible interpretation of these disparate numbers is that models are drawing from their own knowledge bases instead of reasoning from scratch. Whether this is cheating or the models simply working as intended might be more a matter of philosophical debate.
Mark Hinkle, founder of the AIE Network consultancy, suspects the issue of integrity may go deeper.
"Private code doesn't stop reward hacking, it changes the shortcut," he wrote to The Register on LinkedIn.

"On public code the agent goes and finds the answer somebody has already published. On private code there's no answer to find, so it satisfies whatever is checking it. I treat these things like entry-level employees, and a sharp new hire figures out fast what the boss actually looks at."

JetBrains did not immediately respond to a request for comment, but concluded in its post that more investigation is needed. It promises that its people will pore over the open source results to see if any have been contaminated by the LLMs' own memory. It also plans to run its own static analysis tool, Qodana, against the results to check for errors.
Sireesha Pulipati, a staff data engineer and AI observer, suggested, also by LinkedIn, that JetBrains may have needed more specificity in its agent instructions.

"Out of the box [an agent] tends to reach for generic patterns. But when we give it instructions and skills that tell it where to look for our patterns and context, it follows them. A well-controlled harness, with those standards built in, is what makes the agent useful," Pulipati wrote.
So good on JetBrains for providing Kotlin users some information about working with AI, but, as always, AI benchmarks should be approached with extreme side-eye. ®

053968f790922cfd: Unsurprisingly, we’re already seeing some solid Black Friday deals on a wide variety of e-readers. Everything from the Kobo Libra Colour to last-gen Kindle Paperwhite is on sale, but if you’re looking for something much cheaper — or considerably smaller — the Xteink X4 Classic is in a league of its own. Thankfully, the tiny e-reader is down to a new low of $54.87 ($55 off) at Amazon, making it an especially affordable alternative to Amazon’s latest Kindle.

The X4 Classic is an updated version of Xteink’s original pocket-sized e-reader, one that features a miniature 4.3-inch E Ink display that makes it more pocketable than any current Kindle or Kobo model. Like the pricier X4 Pro — which also happens to be on sale direct from Xteink for $84 — it features both physical page-turning buttons and magnets that let you attach it to compatible smartphones. At just 2.4 ounces and 4.9mm thick, it’s also easy to slip into a pocket, while its larger 920mAh battery can last up to 10 days on a single charge.

That said, unlike the X4 Pro, the Classic lacks a touchscreen and built-in reading light, meaning you’ll need an external light to read in the dark. It also uses a proprietary magnetic charging connector instead of USB-C, and transferring books isn’t as straightforward as on a Kindle or Kobo. However, like the Pro, it does support the excellent CrossPoint Reader software, which you can install yourself to improve the reading experience. You can even use it to read books borrowed through Libby or purchased from stores like Kobo, though it takes a few extra steps to do so. Still, if you want an inexpensive, distraction-free way to read on the go, the X4 Classic is hard to beat for less than half the price of a Kindle.

0c810e79880a8f96: <!--kg-card-end: html--> You don’t really realize how much downtime there is in the song “Sandstorm” by Darude until you’re waiting for the bass to drop while it’s playing inside your vagina.

In August 2025, I got an email with the subject line “‘Airpods for your @ss’ raises nearly half a million in Kickstarter campaign.” I get a lot of zany pitches for products that don’t exist yet, and a lot of pitches for products that do exist but perhaps should not. This one was for a device called the Groove Thing, a sex toy that turns music into vibration patterns. But the pitch didn’t include the phrase “sex toy” at all. Instead, it’s called an “internal music player.”

I asked for a unit to review, expecting this to be purely conceptual. But they had one, and offered to send it. “The prototype functions very similarly to the final product but we do want to stress it’s a garage built prototype,” the rep for Groove Thing told me. I thought for a moment about putting something “garage built” and connected to a wall outlet into an orifice and passed. While others were braver, I decided to wait until the version they planned to send to customers in the fall was ready.

The production-ready Groove Thing arrived at my doorstep last month in an intimidatingly large box. The configuration consists of a fairly hefty speaker that’s meant to sit on your nightstand, an AC power cable, and a “resonator base,” which connects to the speaker with a pinned cord. It also came with three attachment shapes: vaginal, anal, and external (a vac-u-lock adapter is available separately for attaching your own dildos to the base). The attachment shapes are made of hard plastic, not the soft, flexible silicone I’m used to in a sex toy. They lock onto the resonator with a twist.

Opening the box and feeling the hard, inflexible plastic raised my skepticism that this thing would be comfortable. Most sex toys are covered in silky silicone that offers a little flexibility and give. But as I’m told over and over by the pamphlets that come in the box, Groove Thing “isn’t a vibrator.” Groove Thing inventor Michael Weiss-Malik, who co-founded it with Elizabeth Dell, told me it’s hard plastic for a reason, and is the result of testing feedback from the around 180 people they handed a prototype before putting it on the market.

“We started with off-the-shelf silicone dongs, and they were already producing an interesting experience for people,” Weiss-Malik told me on a call. “But we experimented with different types of materials, and what we found was that the silicone transmitted way fewer ranges and frequencies than hard plastic, and the hard plastic produces much higher fidelity.”

The mechanism that vibrates the base to the beat of the music is also different from most other sex toys on the market today, Weiss-Malik said. But he declined to share what actually runs the toy, beyond mysteriously stating it’s not “a motor.” Weiss-Malik is a former NASA engineer, where he worked on the software that helped map Mars. He’s also worked at Google, where he worked on Earth mapping software, and previously worked leadership roles at Uber and Cruise, the self-driving car company General Motors later acquired and ultimately shut down after a serious accident. But he’s been involved in the sex positive community in the San Francisco bay area “for going on 20 years,” he told me, and is the type of guy to pop into a sex shop anytime he passes one when traveling. All of this taken together makes a lot of sense to me, given that he’s also the kind of guy to spend a summer between jobs tinkering in his garage, designing a device that could put music up your ass.
Why Are Sex Toy Vibration Patterns So Terrible?
The quest for answers about how vibrator modes are tested and designed.

“Groove Thing doesn't use a motor. We don't say what is in there, but it's not a motor,” he said. “It uses a different set of physics that's more similar to audio equipment, and as a result, it can actually reproduce a full sound form, not just an on-off. You know, a sound-responsive vibrator is mostly just an on-off switch that's connecting to the beat.” Other vibrating sex toys work in that way: An eccentric rotating mass motor spins, turning pre-programmed patterns into vibration. Handheld sex toy makers have to work around several factors, including the limits of these motors, the tendency of soft silicone to dampen vibration, and the shapes they need to compact them into to fit in a device that doesn’t wear out customers’ wrists. Groove Thing seems to get around some of these problems by skipping the typical rotating motor, shaping the attachments in such a way that you can insert them and then go mostly hands-free when lying down, and choosing a plastic that feels kind of awkward at first.

The combination means different instruments and ranges come through as different levels of vibration. “A piano or bass guitar feels different than a drum kit. It almost feels like having a third ear,” Weiss-Malik said. “There's a level of fidelity there, where you have a whole new dimension to the sound that you're hearing. It works particularly well in bass, but it works all the way up to the mid frequencies.” Groove Thing replicates frequencies you can’t hear with your ears, he said — kind of like being at a concert and standing close enough to the stack that you feel it in your chest. As someone who recently almost lost their eyebrows and gained tinnitus at a Mogwai show, I get it, and I think for most people this comparison is what will make the Groove Thing click for them.

”Some of what you're feeling is subsonic; it's down below 20 hertz, and we actually reproduce that as well,” Weiss-Malik said. “So you actually experience parts of your music that you never even noticed were there before, or that your ears can't hear, and that at the very least, home stereo equipment has a very hard time reproducing. So you're getting an experience that hundreds of thousands of dollars worth of speakers are normally required for you to get that out of the recording.” This was my experience with “Sandstorm.” You wouldn’t believe how much not-music is going on in that song, but also, how the moments that seem like they should be intense rumbly bass-drops are actually at a higher register.

The creators of Groove Thing want you to be able to play whatever you want, which you can from your phone via Bluetooth or the optional aux jack, but they also really, really want you to try their intro playlist, I assume to prevent people like myself from putting “Crab Rave” on the stereo and then writing it off as a bust. That playlist is eclectic, beginning with “Beads on the Wind: The Human Experience Remix” and “Aya,” which I would place in a repeat-Burning-Man-attendee genre (no judgement here), but continues into “Blinding Lights” by The Weeknd and, to my pleasant surprise, an underrated track from Taylor Swift’s Lover album, “I Think He Knows.” An additional playlist with more songs features mostly EDM but also throws “Piece of Me” by Britney Spears in there.

This entire test run of this not-vibrator made me, an admittedly tone deaf and musically unsophisticated person (see the previous lines), realize how much is happening in music that I’m never picking up with my own two ears. The “third ear” analogy is pretty spot-on: To enjoy the Groove Thing with an open mind, you have to let go of the typical expectations of other sex tech. Climax isn’t the point. The point is to use your junk to go on a musical journey, which is something that will resonate strongly for some, and miss others.

“You know, people don’t go to a concert just to hear the finale and go home. Groove Thing isn’t a tool like most vibrators are,” Weiss-Malik told me. “It's more like a concert experience. You get to bask in pleasure for a period of time. In our early beta tester groups, the most people who had unlimited usage of it used it for over an hour in their first session. Most of the second time users in that beta group also used it for over an hour in their second session.”

The entire sex tech market has been trending away from the literal, anatomical, and climax-centered for years, with more toys coming in abstracted colors, shapes, and features that focus on pleasure and experience over getting your own personal money shot. I see Groove Thing as a logical step in that evolution.
Groove Thing is shipping out orders as of this month, and retails at $369 for the single unit and more for add-ons and additional units for partnered play.

5a3b624c2bc565c0: Consumer spending has stayed healthy in large part because Americans are staying employed, whether through formal or gig work. AP Photo/David ZalubowskiHoliday shopping season is kicking off, inundating consumers with Black Friday offers. With inflation fatigue, declining real wages and stock market turbulence thrown into the mix, is the U.S. consumer on the verge of scaling back? This question has long puzzled economists, who wonder why spending has held up even as consumer sentiment slumps. As a researcher of supply chains who has also worked for years at consumer products companies, I’ve run my own studies and have been surprised, time and again, by how spending has continued at a healthy clip even when the economy is faltering. Most recently, in March 2026, I built a model to assess how the Iran war could affect global supply chains at three, six and nine months out. In the case of consumer behavior, the hit was less than what was expected. Even though Americans were paying substantially more at the gas pump due to the disruption in the Strait of Hormuz, as well as dealing with tariff-induced inflation and high interest rates, consumer spending held up remarkably well. I now believe I missed two things: resilience and innovation. More specifically, Americans are continuing to work, whether in formal or gig jobs, and that’s the main factor holding up spending. And as long as consumers have income, they’ll keep finding a way. What’s changing, though, is that this balancing act is getting harder for many people to keep up. What resilience looks like Resilience and innovation may sound admirable, but in practice they’re often difficult and onerous. Under “innovation,” some traditional adjustments for consumers include buying cheaper “private label” or store brands, shopping at off-brand and discount stores, or relentlessly hunting for deals. Other adjustments include eating more meals at home rather than going out, or downsizing vacation plans. “Resilience,” meanwhile, can mean taking on extra work. Economists call this the added worker effect, and it shows up during tough times. During the 2007-09 Great Recession, for example, more married women joined the labor force as unemployment rose among their spouses. In 2026, there’s an uptick in retirees heading back to work as well as an increase in the share of mothers with children who are staying in or reentering the workforce. These are both responses to the rising cost of living. More broadly, Americans are using traditional and nontraditional means to make some extra cash. About 1 in 3 workers has had a side hustle in 2026, according to the jobs database ZipRecruiter – whether it’s nanny jobs, side gigs on Etsy, delivering meals for DoorDash or driving customers for Uber. For many Americans, this work is a necessity, not just a way to earn extra discretionary cash. The increasing need for extra work over the past five years underscores the drop in purchasing power from the salaries many people earn. More Americans, including retirees in need of extra income, are taking up gig work, like driving for Uber. AP Photo/Emily Wang Fujiyama Another form of resilience can be seen through volunteering and charitable giving. In my own neighborhood, a food bank that started during the COVID-19 pandemic has helped many in the community over the past five years. Across the country, food bank donations and charitable giving continue to rise despite economic challenges. According to Giving USA, charitable giving rose to US$617 billion in 2025, surpassing the $600 billion mark for the first time. This increase addresses a growing need for food banks to feed Americans who can’t afford basic groceries anymore. At the same time, the actual number of donors is dropping. Shoppers are hitting the limit Many consumers are now running out of levers to pull. Wealthier Americans are continuing to spend at a strong clip, which is why official consumer spending data suggests the economy is steady. But it’s a different picture for the rest. One in four families are spending more than they make, as seen by rising credit delinquency and auto repossessions, according to the Atlanta Federal Reserve. Whether it’s food, healthcare, rent or cars, Americans are spending a much larger share of their income on necessities than they did 10 years ago. For especially strapped Americans, like those facing the double whammy of a car payment and a student loan, these trade-offs are especially challenging. A good example are auto loan delinquencies, now near a 10-year high. Losing a car can mean losing a job, with devastating financial consequences. Frontline workers also miss more shifts as gas prices rise. And this gets to a core lesson for understanding today’s economy: The bedrock for consumer spending remains employment. The stable job market we see right now – with unemployment at 4.1% – is critical. If this healthy job market holds and interest rates and energy prices ultimately ease, the average consumer will still tread water. But if inflation continues to run hotter than the Federal Reserve would like, and rates rise, Americans’ disposable income will likely shrink – and hurt economic growth in the process. That could lead to a domino effect: Unemployment rises, reducing the discretionary spending that had been keeping economic growth steady. Whether it comes to this, it’s important to remember that the holiday season isn’t necessarily an accurate forward-looking indicator. Shoppers often go to great lengths to make family and friends happy. The big challenge for consumers will start in early 2027. Will the Fed hike rates? Will inflation stay high? Will gas prices come down? Until these questions are answered, we’re in the “bend but don’t break” phase. Many consumers are facing challenging times in 2026, but their resilience has been a surprise on the upside. I’d like to be surprised again in 2027 – but that’s far from a sure thing. Chris Gaffney has received funding from the U.S. Department of Commerce's Economic Development Administration.
f10c2d4186bda7b9: PETALING JAYA: A number of Progressive Democratic Party (PDP) members in Bawang Assan have quit the party, following its former senior vice-president, Wong Soon Koh, who left two days ago.

The members were from five "service committees" in the state constituency, which Gabungan Parti Sarawak (GPS) has allocated to the Sarawak United Peoples' Party (SUPP) to contest in the Dec 12 state election.
The members said they joined PDP with Wong believing that this would strengthen GPS and allow them to work for the betterment of Sarawakians, Borneo Post reported.
"However, our experience over time has gradually led to disappointment with PDP's internal political direction, teamwork, and the way grassroots members have been treated.

This was despite GPS officially taking a neutral stand in the elections.
They said Sarawak's political interests should always be the priority.
Wong and other members joined PDP en masse in 2024 following the dissolution of his former party, Parti Sarawak Bersatu (PSB).
However, he exited the party on Monday, saying it had strayed from the political direction that led him to join it.
He nonetheless declared support for GPS and its chairman, Abang Johari Openg, and said he would not be defending the Bawang Assan seat.
Wong, 84, first won Bawang Assan in 1991 under SUPP, where he was a senior leader.
He retained the seat under SUPP in 2011 before leaving the party in 2014 following internal disputes to form the BN-friendly United People's Party (UPP).
In December 2018, UPP rebranded itself as PSB and contested the 2021 Sarawak election as an opposition party.

e6ea2d749ddbc7d9: Win4Wine is one of the more remarkable and creative hacks we've read about in recent years. It runs Windows XP's genuine Explorer shell through patched Wine on Debian 13, with a custom window manager integrating Linux applications into the desktop.
As its GitHub repository explains: "The taskbar, Start menu, desktop and folder windows are XP's real ones, and Linux applications get XP's frames and taskbar buttons."

This impressive, possibly demented project has English installation instructions and a README, although its design documents are in Japanese. We found Mozilla's built-in translation handled those pretty well.
Its developer goes by miKuta0407 on GitHub, their homepage, and X.

Also note, you're going to need some Windows installation media for the full experience. The README says: "No Microsoft files are included. Only the files that are needed are extracted locally from your own ISO."

It supports Windows XP Professional SP3 installation images in 32-bit Japanese or English editions, with an experimental option for Windows 7 SP1 x64. Without either Windows image, it can download and use ReactOS's free software shell instead, for what it terms "a Windows 2000-like classic look." In our view, that sounds much better anyway.

Before any former Windows users cry hurray and reach for an optical drive, this is not some ready-to-run project. The top of the README warns: "This is a personal, experimental project, not a finished product for daily use." The developer has tested it only on a fresh Debian 13 installation and recommends a VM or spare machine, rather than an existing working desktop, which sounds like an excellent precaution to us.
Also, before you ask, yes, it was vibe-coded with Claude.

We found ourselves reminded of another crazy-but-is-it project that we wrote about back in January: What if Linux ran Windows... and meant it? Meet Loss32. The Loss32 proposal was even more extreme. It suggested replacing essentially the entire Linux userland, so it would be a Linux kernel running Wine with a Windows desktop and Windows apps.

However, Mikuta-san was way ahead of us – lower down, the README mentions and even links to Loss32. Saying that, since it launched at the end of 2025, the bottom of the Loss32 web page shows a couple of updates, reporting on delays in getting it working. That, to be honest, did not shock us, but we still admire the let's-do-this spirit. The developer also seems to have got slightly distracted by a previous project, touchHLE: high-level emulator for early iOS apps.

Loss32, in turn, reminded us of Neptune OS, an attempt to give seL4 a Windows personality transplant. We wrote about that back in 2022, and work on it has continued: the project page shows updates in recent months. The team has also pushed out preview releases in 2022, 2024, 2025, and most recently in September.

This OS face transplant also reminded us of our article, Classic 7 is Windows 10 LTSC cosplaying as Windows 7. Some people really miss the look and feel of vintage Windows. Can someone do Windows NT 4 next, please? ®

AI has intensified investors’ interest in public records. Over the last few years, venture-backed startups have raised upwards of $100 million to collect data from thousands of agencies and turn it into AI-powered “signals” that help businesses sell to governments. At the same time, chatbots are making it easier for individuals to file requests.

As agencies struggle to tell whether they’re dealing with a citizen, a chatbot, or a sales pipeline, some states are passing legislation that makes it easier to deny requests. That could potentially make public offices less transparent.

MIT Technology Review Narrated: Inside the quest to combat Arctic fires and save the planet’s frozen carbon

In July 2021, a wildfire burned through a forest on the University of Alaska, Fairbanks campus, stripping away the moss and soil insulating the permafrost below. Five years later, we followed researchers into the forest to investigate how fighting fires could help keep that carbon locked in the ground.

Their probe revealed an escalating problem: As climate change fuels more frequent and severe fires, they’re accelerating permafrost thaw and releasing greenhouse gases. Now, researchers are trying to break that cycle. But how much should we spend, and what risks are worth taking?

This is our latest story to become an MIT Technology Review Narrated podcast, which we publish each week on Spotify and Apple Podcasts. Just navigate to MIT Technology Review Narrated on either platform, and follow us to get all our new content as it’s released.

Kids outlearn AI—and we still don’t know why

This yawning divide between children and machines is called the data efficiency gap. It raises a tantalizing question for researchers: How can children learn so much with so little?

By reverse-engineering how they learn, scientists hope to create more efficient AI models—and perhaps settle enduring questions about language and children’s developing minds. Here’s how they’re trying to close the data gap.

351fcb70185fd42b: NOVEMBER 25 — For 17 years, before I faced the demands of each day, there was Ninja.

Every morning after prayer, I would talk to him. He never answered in words, but his familiar presence was enough. My life has been shaped by discipline, ambition and responsibility, and Ninja gave me something no achievement could measure: peace.

He was there through uncertain beginnings, changing fortunes and ordinary nights whose worth I only understood later. He was family, my most loyal companion and the quiet presence beside me through everything.

On November 18, Ninja turned 17. He spent his birthday receiving a blood transfusion while his veterinary team worked to support him through a complex illness. Two days later, at 1.20am on November 20, he died in my arms. I held him on my chest until dawn.

Ninja had been under veterinary care for close to a month, first at private facilities and later at Universiti Putra Malaysia’s (UPM) veterinary hospital. He had severe anaemia, kidney abnormalities, breathing difficulties and fluid accumulation. His treatment included oxygen support, assisted feeding, medication and a blood transfusion, and the bills came to more than RM30,000.
Despite all of that, he could not be saved.

I remember him as a fighter. He was a small companion who kept enduring setbacks while staying deeply connected to me. It comforts me to think he stayed until his work as my companion was done. That is how I make sense of our farewell, after 17 years in which he gave me the strength to face so much.

What remains is grief, and also a responsibility I feel towards other animals. I want Ninja’s story to help other owners notice changes in their cats, understand why veterinary tests are done and ask informed questions about their cats’ care.

Earlier assessment cannot guarantee recovery, and a difficult outcome does not prove an illness could have been prevented. But noticing changes and investigating them quickly can create chances for treatment and management.

Older cats can develop several conditions at once, so changes in their behaviour or physical condition should not automatically be put down to age. Common problems include chronic kidney disease, hyperthyroidism, diabetes, hypertension, dental disease, arthritis and cancer.
Five groups of changes deserve particular attention:

Appetite or weight changes. Eating less, difficulty chewing or unexplained weight loss should be checked. A cat that stops eating needs prompt veterinary advice, because even 24 hours without food can have serious consequences.
Increased thirst or changes in urination. More drinking, larger litter clumps or new toileting accidents can come with several illnesses. Repeated straining with little or no urine is an emergency.
Changes in movement, grooming or behaviour. Reluctance to jump, stiffness, hiding, irritability or an unkempt coat may point to pain or illness.
Persistent vomiting, diarrhoea or bowel changes. Symptoms that keep coming back need investigation, especially alongside poor appetite or weight loss.
Breathing difficulty, collapse or marked weakness. These need urgent assessment. Laboured or open-mouth breathing should never wait for a routine appointment.
One of the most important lessons I learnt is the value of knowing what is being tested, what the results mean and what should happen next.
A senior-cat assessment begins with a thorough physical examination. Common investigations include:
- A complete blood count to check for anaemia and blood-cell abnormalities
- Blood chemistry to look at kidney and liver markers, glucose, proteins and electrolytes
- Urinalysis
- A total T4 thyroid test
- Blood-pressure measurement

These tests complement one another, but they are not a universal panel that rules out every illness. Depending on the findings, imaging, cultures, fluid analysis or other targeted tests may be needed. Keeping previous results lets vets look at trends instead of relying on a single reading. Senior cats generally benefit from check-ups at least every six months, more often depending on their condition.

Feline infectious peritonitis (FIP) was among the conditions suspected during Ninja’s treatment, but it has not been established as the cause of his death. A positive feline coronavirus antibody test alone does not diagnose FIP.

Among the memories I carry from those last days is the response to our urgent appeal for blood donors. About 14 cats were brought forward by their owners, many of them strangers. Some travelled long distances. Some arrived late at night and waited while arrangements were made. They offered their time and their own companions in the hope of helping mine.
I thank every owner who came forward, Doctors and the UPM staff who cared for Ninja, and everyone who shared the appeal or kept my family in their prayers. Their kindness is part of Ninja’s story.
So is the lesson of his life: loyalty is often quiet, companionship can steady a person through years of uncertainty, and care begins with paying attention.
No one can fill Ninja’s place in my life, and my mornings are different now. But the conversations after prayer will go on, beside the place where he rests.
If his story leads another owner to notice a change, get an examination or better understand a treatment plan, part of his legacy will live on there too.
Seventeen years of companionship have ended. The care it inspired does not have to.
• Murad Zaidi is a high-performance coach.

327350700c1cab32: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 25 — Safiah (not her real name) initially dismissed a small lump, about the size of a 20-sen coin, on her calf as a pus-filled boil and sought treatment at a private clinic, where a procedure was performed to drain the pus.
However, not long after the procedure, the lump reappeared and continued to grow, prompting the woman in her 50s to return to the same clinic to have the entire growth removed.
Unfortunately, the attempt only made matters worse, as the lump grew bigger, protruding above the skin in a cauliflower-like appearance and began to bleed. Her body also became increasingly weak.

She was eventually referred to Hospital Canselor Tuanku Muhriz (HCTM), Universiti Kebangsaan Malaysia (UKM), where further investigations confirmed that the lump was actually a rare form of cancer known as sarcoma.
Soft tissue and bone cancer

HCTM Orthopaedic Oncology Consultant at the Department of Orthopaedics and Traumatology, Dr Mohamed Hafizudin Abdullah Sani, said sarcoma is a group of cancers distinct from carcinoma, the more commonly recognised type of cancer.
“Carcinoma originates from epithelial cells that line the surfaces or organs of the body, whereas sarcoma develops from mesenchymal cells, which form various supporting tissues in the body.
“This cancer can affect soft tissues such as muscles, fat and blood vessels, as well as bones, depending on the type of cells and tissues involved,” he told Bernama.

Elaborating, he said soft tissue sarcomas were often more difficult to detect in their early stages because some tumours do not cause pain. In fact, some may grow slowly over several months or even longer.
Pain usually develops only when the tumour becomes larger and starts pressing against nearby structures, he added.

“Among the warning signs to look out for are a growing lump that feels firm or hard, is located deep within the tissue and measures more than five centimetres (about the size of a golf ball or a small Grade A egg).

“Physical changes on the skin’s surface, such as tightness, redness or a bluish discolouration, as well as increasingly visible superficial blood vessels, may also indicate the need for further medical assessment,” he said.
Bone sarcoma, meanwhile, presents differently, with patients typically experiencing pain in the affected bone before noticeable swelling develops.
However, he stressed that these characteristics do not necessarily confirm cancer, but should be regarded as warning signs warranting prompt medical attention.
The pitfalls of ‘whoops surgery’ and tissue contamination

Dr Mohamed Hafizudin said one of the challenges in managing sarcoma was the removal of a tumour before the cancer had been properly diagnosed, a procedure known among specialists as an “unplanned excision” or “whoops surgery”.

“‘Whoops surgery’ refers to a situation where a tumour is removed without proper oncological planning, potentially contaminating the surgical area with tumour cells. It is like trying to clean up a dirty area but ending up spreading the dirt everywhere.

“As a result, specialists may find it difficult to identify which areas of tissue have been exposed to tumour cells, and the patient may require another operation involving a wider area of tissue removal,” he explained.

Citing Safiah’s case, he said the procedure performed at the private clinic before she was referred to HCTM had not followed the specialised surgical approach required for sarcoma, making it more difficult for the medical team to determine the actual extent of tissue that needed to be removed.
By the time she was referred to HCTM, the tumour had grown considerably and involved both soft tissue and bone, making surgical planning more challenging.

“Sarcoma surgery requires meticulous planning as the tumour must be removed together with an adequate margin of healthy tissue (wide excision), while also taking into account the possibility of satellite nodules or reactive areas surrounding it.
“Satellite nodules can be likened to seeds or roots growing around the main tumour, and these must be considered when determining the extent of tumour removal,” he explained.
He stressed that suspicious lumps should first undergo proper medical assessment before any removal procedure is carried out.

Asked about the factors contributing to ‘whoops surgery’, Dr Mohamed Hafizudin said this could happen because some general practitioners (GPs) at clinics were not sufficiently aware of sarcoma and its early warning signs.
As such, he said HCTM had been actively working to raise awareness through public awareness programmes, symposiums and specialised workshops for GPs.

“The initiative aims to help medical practitioners recognise suspicious signs and make early referrals to tertiary centres with the relevant expertise, thereby reducing the risk of inappropriate procedures before a sarcoma diagnosis is established,” he added.
Caseload challenges and the success of limb salvage

Revisiting Safiah’s case, he said amputation had initially been considered before a multidisciplinary team opted for a complex surgical approach to remove the tumour and reconstruct the affected area in an effort to preserve her limb.

“Following the successful surgery, a small portion of the transplanted tissue used to cover the surgical area developed edge necrosis. However, the affected portion eventually healed on its own. She was also able to walk again six weeks after the operation,” he shared.
Dr Mohamed Hafizudin said medical teams treating sarcoma patients would generally make every effort to save the affected limb while preserving its function.

He said the decision to retain a limb depended on several key considerations, including whether the tumour could be removed with a safe margin, the possibility of reconstructing the lost tissue and the ability to preserve or restore limb function by protecting vital structures such as nerves and blood vessels.
“If the tumour cannot be removed with a safe margin or the affected limb is unlikely to retain adequate function after treatment, amputation may still be an appropriate medical option.

“This is because the success of sarcoma treatment should not be measured solely by the removal of the tumour, but also by the patient’s ability to resume daily life with the best possible restoration of limb function,” he added.
On the hospital’s caseload, he said his team handled about two to three sarcoma surgeries each month, amounting to approximately 24 to 25 operations annually.

“However, the reality is that the caseload referred to tertiary centres remains challenging, with the majority of patients being referred at advanced stages due to delays in early detection,” he said. — Bernama
34d13577d448a04d: SAN FRANCISCO, Nov 25 — Californians are preparing for a confluence of exceptionally high tides and El Nino-fuelled weather that threatens coastal areas with extreme flooding during the busiest US travel week of the year.

The San Francisco Bay Area is expected to get hit hard with a one-two punch of inclement weather and monster tides, which forecasters warned could push seawater into low-lying areas on Wednesday and Thursday.

San Francisco International Airport officials said its runways were no longer at risk of flooding, but authorities still urged residents to reconsider travel plans during the Thanksgiving holiday week.
San Francisco Mayor Daniel Lurie warned the situation was “extremely serious.”
Tuesday afternoon, he implored people to avoid driving through flooding that could be triggered by incoming rain that’s expected to start Tuesday evening.
“Do not drive through floodwaters,” the mayor said. “We are hoping by the mid- to late afternoon the tides will have subsided considerably.”
So-called king tides occur every year due to the gravitational pull and alignments of the Earth, Moon and Sun. They will occur again in December and January.
The ocean is also hotter than usual — and thus increasing in volume — both due to human-caused climate change and this year’s exceptionally strong El Nino weather pattern.
The ocean warming phenomenon in the central and eastern equatorial Pacific has already altered weather around the world, resulting in devastating droughts and wildfires.
Dial Hoang at the National Weather Service (NWS) told AFP that the Bay Area could see up to nearly three feet of flooding when the tides peak Wednesday.
The agency said in a bulletin that dangerously large breaking waves up to 30 feet could hit California’s coast on Wednesday, with hazardous beach conditions persisting through Sunday.
Just the beginning
This year’s tides are predicted to be at their highest levels since January 1983, Hoang said.
Those tides also coincided with vicious, El Nino-fueled storms — and the impact was catastrophic.

“All hell broke loose,” said Reinhard Flick, a coastal oceanographer at University of California, San Diego’s Scripps Institution. “We had 13-foot waves offshore, the highest tides of the year, and hundreds of millions of dollars in damage.”
The state might not see the same level of destruction this week, thanks to storm preparedness and infrastructure improvements.
Dangers still remain. Strong winds could fell trees, Mayor Lurie warned, and “low-lying streets along the waterfront can flood with little to no rain.”
After a storm caused major flooding across San Francisco last week, residents and business owners were anxiously preparing for another possible deluge.
“We closed the door thinking that should be sufficient but it wasn’t,” Eric Im told AFP on Tuesday.
His family’s restaurant, Jim Georgie’s Donuts, was flooded last week after the heavy rain overwhelmed the city’s sewage system. Now they have sand bags ready.
In the city’s Marina district, which hugs the coastline near the Golden Gate Bridge, residents were also placing sandbags outside their homes on Tuesday.
“We’re hoping for the best, but we’re not too worried,” one resident, who identified herself only as Heather, told AFP.
In Southern California, forecasters warned that sneaker waves could wash beachgoers out to sea, and surge into parking lots or roadways.
“Always keep an eye on the ocean,” the NWS said. “Waves can run up much further than expected, do not assume dry spots are safe.” — AFP
59fd20b70113bf7d: SAINT-OUEN (France), Nov 25 — Long disregarded as a bland, soggy mess, the humble French egg mayonnaise is making a comeback — with gourmets awarding a special prize to a young chef’s partly plant-based version.
The World Egg Mayonnaise Championship crowned Hugo Riboulet, co-founder of Paris restaurant Groot La Tourte, who beat the cream of the contenders at a ceremony near the French capital on Monday.
His dish featured confit egg yolk, with puffed spelt grains for texture and served on a jelly made from the tart juice of unripe grapes.
“I have a plant-based approach to cooking and I tried to recreate that, to think about it as a Michelin-starred dish,” said Riboulet, 2023 winner of the Top Chef television competition.
“The idea is not to add fat on top of fat or to keep piling on animal protein.”
The competition is organised by the Association for the Preservation of Egg Mayonnaise (ASOM), a bistro lobby group working to whisk the dish back onto menus.
For decades, it was associated with “undercooked eggs with bland industrial mayonnaise”, said the event’s organiser, Foulques de Penguilly.
But in recent years it has begun to appear in trendy restaurants in New York, California and Tokyo.
Now the award will have customers scrambling for reservations.
“Your bookings fill up right away,” said last year’s winner, Mathieu Renucci, the chef at Paris bistro Au Reve.
“You’ll be serving that dish thousands of times.” — AFP
dea01f50cdabdb1d: BERLIN, Nov 25 — Germany’s consumer protection association said Tuesday it would take legal action against Meta and the makers of Ray-Ban over data privacy concerns linked to AI-powered smart glasses.
Ramona Pop, head of the Federation of German Consumer Organizations (vzbv), said the wearable devices “make it possible to record images and audio unnoticed”.
“Smart glasses create significant data protection risks both for bystanders and for users themselves,” she said.
The vzbv argued that potential buyers of the glasses were not sufficiently informed that their use could be in breach of the European General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR).
“Products must be designed in such a way that people can use them in compliance with data protection rules and the rights of third parties remain protected,” said Pop.
Smart glasses are being sold by various eyewear manufacturers in cooperation with technology companies, with the capacity to take photos, videos, and audio recordings, as well as livestreams.

Manufacturers say that LED lights on the glasses prevent people nearby from being filmed without noticing, but consumer advocates argue that this is insufficient to protect consumers from unwanted recordings.
“A tiny white blinking light just a few millimetres in size is not enough to signal to people in public spaces that they are being filmed,” said Pop.

The association said it had filed a lawsuit against Ray-Ban manufacturer EssilorLuxottica in a Berlin court and that it plans to take similar action against US tech giant Meta - which owns WhatsApp, Facebook and Instagram.
Neither company was immediately available for comment. — AFP
151e110ad0ba17ed: SYDNEY: Australia's corporate regulator said on Wednesday it has discovered dozens of additional cases of suspected audit misconduct among the Big Four accounting firms, ranging from misuse of client information to falsified work.

The Australian Securities and Investments Commission (ASIC) said it was now considering its enforcement and regulatory options following its review of 558 audit complaints at KPMG, PwC, Deloitte and EY.

The Big Four have been beset by a number of scandals in recent years. The latest has KPMG under regulatory and political investigation after whistleblower allegations came to light this year, accusing the firm of sharing confidential audit client information to bid for more work with other companies.
The Australian government is considering breaking up the Big ​Four firms and imposing partnership size caps as well as stipulating a mandatory rotation of audit firms in a bid to clean up the sector.
ASIC's review, announced in July, required the firms to hand over internal documents dating back to July 2023. The Big Four recorded 3,215 internal complaints during the three-year period.
Of the 558 audit complaints ASIC examined, 35 raised questions about "the conduct of a statutory audit, or the misuse of statutory audit client information", the review found.
"The most common concerns involved audit work that had been falsified, inaccurately documented or recorded without adequate evidence," ASIC said.
A number of complaints alleged employees were directed to disregard, conceal or not escalate issues identified during an audit or that, when escalated, the issues were not investigated appropriately.
"There was also misuse and sharing of confidential statutory audit client information, including during an audit tender process," ASIC said.
"Some of the complaints included serious allegations of misconduct that are under consideration for enforcement action," ASIC's report said.
Other issues related to matters currently being investigated by ASIC, including its existing KPMG probe.
ASIC criticised the firms' internal responses to the complaints, finding they had investigated a number of concerns as workplace matters instead of audit quality issues.

It also said the majority of firms initially engaged with its inquiries in a "protracted and legalistic" way, withholding or redacting documents, making extensive legal privilege claims and missing deadlines.
KPMG said in a statement it was considering ASIC's report and how it could help the firm improve its processes.
"We are also progressing a number of measures to further strengthen our speak-up culture," KPMG said.
PwC also said it was considering the report, and that audit quality was its highest priority.
"We take complaints raised seriously and are continuously improving our processes and practices," a spokesperson said.
Deloitte said it welcomed ASIC's ongoing work to maintain trust in the profession.
EY did not immediately respond to a request for comment.
Scale of misconduct 'alarming'
"What a shameful list of failures," Deborah O'Neill, a senator from the ruling Labor Party who made the whistleblower allegations against KPMG public in March, said in a statement.
"It's clearer than ever that the barrel contains more than just a few bad apples," she said.
Greens senator Barbara Pocock said the "sheer scale of misconduct within the Big 4 is alarming", calling for ASIC to be given more powers to police the firms.
"The evidence points to a culture of misconduct running right across the Big 4," she said.

"The Big 4 cannot be allowed to continue operating like corporate cowboys, effectively policing themselves while misconduct goes unchecked. We need proper regulation, real oversight and a watchdog with teeth," she added.

The firms are treated as partnerships rather than companies in Australia. That means they are not subject to supervision by ASIC, which has strict reporting requirements, and are instead regulated by state-based ‌laws.
ASIC's powers only extend to individual company auditors.
Commissioner Kate O'Rourke said ASIC would continue to engage with the government on the regulation of audit firms.
"The issues identified through this review reinforce the case for audit firm licensing and stronger enforcement and disciplinary powers," she said.
The KPMG scandal comes three years after it emerged that PwC shared confidential government tax policy details to win clients.

47a9e4632e45bc05: Recovery windows of up to ten years are now available in Microsoft 365 Backup for OneDrive and SharePoint, up from a previous maximum of two.
The change took effect on October 31, though Exchange remains capped at two years.

Administrators can select recovery windows of three months, six months, or any whole number of years from one to ten. Microsoft's list price is $0.15 per GiB per month of protected content. Extended windows can increase costs by keeping deleted data billable for longer.
Switching to a longer recovery window will also not make backups for that period magically available. So no nostalgic trips back to 2016.

Wider recovery windows may appeal to organizations that need access to older data, but backups are not a substitute for compliance retention and archiving. Recovery after a breach or ransomware attack is also critical, particularly getting back to a healthy state before any malware seeped into files.
Microsoft says backups are physically redundant and geographically replicated while respecting the tenant's data residency requirements.
Full OneDrive account and SharePoint site restores offer recovery points every ten minutes for the most recent two weeks, then weekly points through the configured window, up to ten years.
Individual file and folder recovery is limited to recovery points from the most recent 14 days, regardless of the configured window.
Restore remains free, which is handy since regular testing is a vital part of any disaster recovery plan.

The arrival of a ten-year recovery window is good for enterprises that need it and have deep enough pockets. However, it is important to keep in mind that being able to configure a longer recovery window doesn't constitute a disaster recovery plan in itself and may be overkill in many instances.
Microsoft notes: "The existing one-year default recovery window remains unchanged. Longer recovery windows must be configured on the applicable backup policies."
The company also recommends that users "review your organization's SharePoint and OneDrive backup requirements to determine whether longer recovery windows are needed."
A decade of recovery history could be valuable. It also means a decade of data to account for when setting budgets, access controls, and retention policies. ®

907b953824439dcb: BARCELONA, Nov 25 — Real Madrid and Barcelona failed to reach an agreement on Wednesday in a conciliation hearing over statements made by Los Blancos president Florentino Perez regarding the Negreira refereeing scandal, a source from the Catalan club confirmed to AFP.

The hearing followed a lawsuit filed by Barcelona on June 12 against Perez for his statements in May, in which he accused the Spanish champions of scheming to obtain favourable treatment from referees.

“The aim of this lawsuit is for Mr Perez to retract certain statements he made, knowing they were false, which are defamatory and offensive to the club’s image and reputation,” Barcelona had declared when initiating legal action.
“In the event that this lawsuit is not duly addressed, Barcelona will proceed to file the corresponding criminal complaint for defamation,” Barca added in June.
